"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text

"""PackageBuildInfo class and system resource helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import pathlib
import types
import typing
from collections.abc import Mapping

import psutil
from packaging.utils import BuildTag, NormalizedName
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import overrides, threading_utils
from ._models import (
    GitOptions,
    PackageSettings,
    ProjectOverride,
    PurlConfig,
    VariantInfo,
)
from ._templates import _resolve_template, substitute_template
from ._typedefs import Annotations, PackageVersion, PatchMap, Template, Variant

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import build_environment
    from ._settings import Settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _default_is_pre_built(*, version: Version, variant: Variant) -> None:
    """Defer the pre-built setting to package YAML."""
    return None


def get_available_memory_gib() -> float:
    """available virtual memory in GiB"""
    return psutil.virtual_memory().available / (1024**3)


class PackageBuildInfo:
    """Package build information

    Public API for PackageSettings with i
    """

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, ps: PackageSettings) -> None:
        self._variant = typing.cast(Variant, settings.variant)
        self._patches_dir = settings.patches_dir
        self._variant_changelog = settings.variant_changelog()
        self._max_jobs: int | None = settings.max_jobs
        self._ps = ps
        self._plugin_module: types.ModuleType | typing.Literal[False] | None = False
        self._patches: PatchMap | None = None
        self._annotations: Annotations | None = None

    @property
    def package(self) -> NormalizedName:
        """Package name"""
        return typing.cast(NormalizedName, self._ps.name)

    @property
    def variant(self) -> Variant:
        """Variant name"""
        return self._variant

    @property
    def purl_config(self) -> PurlConfig | None:
        """Per-package purl configuration for SBOM generation."""
        return self._ps.purl

    @property
    def annotations(self) -> Annotations:
        """Get Package and variant annotations

        Annotations can be used to attach arbitrary metadata to packages and
        package variants. The feature is inspired by Kubernetes's
        annotations. Variant keys have a higher precedence than package keys.

        The prefix ``fromager.`` is reserved for future use by Fromager.

        ::

           annotations:
             "downstream.maintainer": "Platform Team"
           variants:
             cuda:
               annotations:
                 "downstream.maintainer": "CUDA Accelerator Team"
        """
        if self._annotations is None:
            vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)
            va = vi.annotations if vi is not None else None
            self._annotations = Annotations(self._ps.annotations, va)
        return self._annotations

    @property
    def plugin(self) -> types.ModuleType | None:
        """Get Fromager plugin module"""
        if self._plugin_module is False:
            exts = overrides._get_extensions()
            try:
                mod = exts[self.override_module_name].plugin
                self._plugin_module = typing.cast(types.ModuleType, mod)
            except KeyError:
                self._plugin_module = None
        return self._plugin_module

    def get_all_patches(self) -> PatchMap:
        """Get a mapping of version to list of patches"""

        if self._patches is None:
            patches: PatchMap = {}
            version: Version | None

            # Find unversioned and versioned directories (name + '-' + version)
            # with patches for the package.
            dirs_to_scan = []
            unversioned_dir = self._patches_dir / self.override_module_name
            if unversioned_dir.exists():
                dirs_to_scan.append(unversioned_dir)
            versioned_pattern = f"{self.override_module_name}-*"
            dirs_to_scan.extend(self._patches_dir.glob(versioned_pattern))

            prefix_len = len(self.override_module_name) + 1
            for patchdir in dirs_to_scan:
                if patchdir.name == self.override_module_name:
                    version = None
                else:
                    version = Version(patchdir.name[prefix_len:])
                patches[version] = list(patchdir.glob("*.patch"))
                # variant-specific patches
                patches[version].extend(patchdir.joinpath(self.variant).glob("*.patch"))
                patches[version].sort(key=lambda p: p.name)

            self._patches = patches
        return self._patches

    def get_patches(self, version: Version) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
        """Get patches for a version (and unversioned patches)"""
        # ignore local version for patches
        version = Version(version.public)
        patchfiles: list[pathlib.Path] = []
        patchmap = self.get_all_patches()
        # unversioned patches
        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(None, []))
        # version-specific patches
        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(version, []))
        # sort by basename
        patchfiles.sort(key=lambda p: p.name)
        return patchfiles

    @property
    def has_config(self) -> bool:
        """Does the package have a config file?"""
        return self._ps.has_config

    @property
    def has_customizations(self) -> bool:
        """Does the package have any customizations?"""
        return bool(
            self.has_config or self.plugin is not None or self.get_all_patches()
        )

    def pre_built(self) -> bool:

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import resolver, sources, wheels
from ..requirements_file import RequirementType
from ._phase import Phase
from ._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from ._types import BootstrapPhase

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import context
    from ._bootstrapper import Bootstrapper

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _re_resolve_url(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType,
    resolved_version: Version,
    pre_built: bool,
    cache_wheel_server_url: str | None,
) -> str | None:
    """Resolve the source or wheel URL selected by version-specific settings."""
    pinned_req = Requirement(f"{req.name}=={resolved_version}")
    if pre_built:
        wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
            ctx,
            pinned_req,
            cache_wheel_server_url=cache_wheel_server_url,
            version=resolved_version,
        )
        try:
            wheel_url, _ = wheels.resolve_prebuilt_wheel(
                ctx=ctx,
                req=pinned_req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        except ExceptionGroup:
            return None
        return str(wheel_url)

    provider = sources.get_source_provider(
        ctx=ctx,
        req=pinned_req,
        sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,
        req_type=req_type,
    )
    matches = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(provider, pinned_req)
    return str(matches[0][0]) if matches else None


class Start(Phase):
    """Record a resolved requirement in the dependency graph and deduplicate.

    Adds the ``(parent → req)`` edge to the dependency graph, then checks
    whether this ``(req, version)`` pair has already been processed.  Duplicate
    requirements are silently dropped; new ones proceed to source preparation.
    ``tracks_why`` is ``False`` so graph additions happen before the why-stack
    is updated.

    Next phase: ``PrepareSource`` (new requirement) or ``[]`` (already seen).
    """

    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.START
    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False

    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:
        """START phase: add to graph, check if already seen.

        _track_why is a no-op for this phase (tracks_why is False),
        matching the original behavior where graph addition and
        seen-check happen before pushing onto the why stack.

        Returns:
            Empty list if already seen (nothing to do).
            [PrepareSource] if this is new work.
        """
        wi = self.work_item
        assert wi.resolved_version is not None
        assert wi.source_url is not None

        pbi = bt.ctx.package_build_info(wi.req)
        wi.pbi_pre_built = pbi.is_pre_built(wi.resolved_version)
        if wi.pbi_pre_built != pbi.pre_built or (
            wi.pbi_pre_built
            and pbi.get_wheel_server_url(wi.resolved_version) != pbi.wheel_server_url
        ):
            logger.info(
                "re-resolving download URL for %s==%s using %s",
                wi.req.name,
                wi.resolved_version,
                "pre-built wheel" if wi.pbi_pre_built else "source distribution",
            )
            resolved_url = _re_resolve_url(
                ctx=bt.ctx,
                req=wi.req,
                req_type=wi.req_type,
                resolved_version=wi.resolved_version,
                pre_built=wi.pbi_pre_built,
                cache_wheel_server_url=bt.cache_wheel_server_url,
            )
            if resolved_url is None:
                logger.warning(
                    "could not re-resolve download URL for %s==%s; keeping %s",
                    wi.req.name,
                    wi.resolved_version,
                    wi.source_url,
                )
            else:
                wi.source_url = resolved_url

        wi.build_sdist_only = bt.sdist_only and not wi.is_build_requirement_context()

        # Add dependency edges, or refresh the pre-added top-level URL.
        if wi.req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:
            bt.add_to_graph(
                wi.req,
                wi.req_type,
                wi.resolved_version,
                wi.source_url,
                wi.parent,
            )
        else:
            bt.ctx.dependency_graph.update_download_url(
                wi.req,
                wi.resolved_version,
                wi.source_url,
            )
            bt._write_graph_async()

        if bt.has_been_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only):
            logger.debug(
                f"redundant {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} "
                f"({wi.resolved_version}, sdist_only={wi.build_sdist_only}) "
                f"for {bt.explain}"
            )
            return []
        bt.mark_as_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only)

        logger.info(
            f"new {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} resolves to {wi.resolved_version}"
        )

        # Must set pbi_pre_built before constructing PrepareSource so that
        # PrepareSource.background_work() immediately sees the correct value.
        wi.exclusive_build = pbi.exclusive_build
        return [PrepareSource(wi)]

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import dataclasses
import graphlib
import json
import logging
import pathlib
import threading
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from .read import open_file_or_url
from .requirements_file import RequirementType

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .context import WorkContext

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

ROOT = ""


class DependencyEdgeDict(typing.TypedDict):
    req_type: str
    req: str
    key: str


class DependencyNodeDict(typing.TypedDict):
    download_url: str
    canonicalized_name: str
    version: str
    pre_built: bool
    # not set in older graph files
    constraint: typing.NotRequired[str | None]
    edges: list[DependencyEdgeDict]


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True)
class DependencyNode:
    canonicalized_name: NormalizedName
    version: Version
    download_url: str = dataclasses.field(default="", compare=False)
    pre_built: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)
    constraint: Requirement | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    # additional fields
    key: str = dataclasses.field(init=False, compare=False, repr=False)
    parents: list[DependencyEdge] = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory=list,
        init=False,
        compare=False,
        repr=False,
    )
    children: list[DependencyEdge] = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory=list,
        init=False,
        compare=False,
        repr=False,
    )

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.canonicalized_name == ROOT:
            # root has a special key
            object.__setattr__(self, "key", ROOT)
        else:
            object.__setattr__(
                self, "key", f"{self.canonicalized_name}=={self.version}"
            )

    @property
    def requirement(self) -> Requirement:
        if self.canonicalized_name == ROOT:
            raise RuntimeError("root node is not a requirement")
        return Requirement(self.key)

    def add_child(
        self,
        child: DependencyNode,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
    ) -> None:
        current_to_child_edge = DependencyEdge(
            req=req, req_type=req_type, destination_node=child
        )
        self.children.append(current_to_child_edge)
        child_to_current_edge = DependencyEdge(
            req=req, req_type=req_type, destination_node=self
        )
        # will create a cyclic dependency in memory, which will make it harder to garbage collect
        # not an issue for fromager since it is used as a short-lived process
        child.parents.append(child_to_current_edge)

    def to_dict(self) -> DependencyNodeDict:
        return {
            "download_url": self.download_url,
            "pre_built": self.pre_built,
            "version": str(self.version),
            "canonicalized_name": str(self.canonicalized_name),
            "constraint": str(self.constraint) if self.constraint else None,
            "edges": [edge.to_dict() for edge in self.children],
        }

    def get_incoming_install_edges(self) -> list[DependencyEdge]:
        return [
            edge for edge in self.parents if edge.req_type == RequirementType.INSTALL
        ]

    def get_outgoing_edges(
        self, req_name: str, req_type: RequirementType
    ) -> list[DependencyEdge]:
        return [
            edge
            for edge in self.children
            if canonicalize_name(edge.req.name) == canonicalize_name(req_name)
            and edge.req_type == req_type
        ]

    @classmethod
    def construct_root_node(cls) -> DependencyNode:
        return cls(
            canonicalize_name(ROOT),
            # version doesn't really matter for root
            Version("0"),
        )

    def iter_build_requirements(self) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyNode]:
        """Get all unique, recursive build requirements

        Yield all direct and indirect requirements to build the dependency.
        Includes direct build dependencies and their recursive **install**
        requirements.

        The result is equivalent to the set of ``[build-system].requires``
        plus all ``Requires-Dist`` of build system requirements -- all
        packages in the build environment.
        """
        visited: set[str] = set()
        # The outer loop iterates over all children and picks
        # direct build requirements. For each build requirement, it traverses
        # all children and recursively get their install requirements
        # (depth first).
        for edge in self.children:
            if edge.key in visited:
                # optimization: don't traverse visited nodes
                continue
            if not edge.req_type.is_build_requirement:
                # not a build requirement
                continue
            visited.add(edge.key)
            # it's a new ``[build-system].requires``.
            yield edge.destination_node
            # recursively get install dependencies of this build dep (depth first).
            for install_edge in self._traverse_install_requirements(
                edge.destination_node.children, visited
            ):
                yield install_edge.destination_node

    def iter_all_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyNode]:
        """Get all unique, recursive dependencies following every edge type.

        Yields every reachable node exactly once using iterative DFS.
        Follows install, build, and toplevel edges.
        """
        visited: set[str] = {self.key}
        stack: list[DependencyNode] = [self]
        while stack:
            current = stack.pop()
            for edge in current.children:
                child_node = edge.destination_node
                if child_node.key in visited:
                    continue
                visited.add(child_node.key)
                yield child_node
                stack.append(child_node)

    def iter_install_requirements(self) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyNode]:
        """Get all unique, recursive install requirements"""
        visited: set[str] = set()
        for edge in self._traverse_install_requirements(self.children, visited):
            yield edge.destination_node

    def _traverse_install_requirements(
        self,
        start_edges: list[DependencyEdge],
        visited: set[str],
    ) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyEdge]:
        # Depth-first walk of install requirement edges, skipping nodes
        # already visited to avoid loops in the dependency graph.
        for edge in start_edges:
            if edge.key in visited:
                continue
            if not edge.req_type.is_install_requirement:
                continue
            visited.add(edge.destination_node.key)
            yield edge

Hooks and Overrides
===================

Fromager has two plugin systems that serve different purposes:
**per-package overrides** replace default behavior for a specific
package, while **global hooks** broadcast notifications after events
for every package.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`/reference/hooks` documents each override hook's arguments and
   return values.  :doc:`/customization` covers global hooks with code
   examples.

Comparison
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 20 40 40

   * - Aspect
     - Per-Package Overrides
     - Global Hooks
   * - **Scope**
     - One named package
     - Every package
   * - **Cardinality**
     - At most one override module per package
     - Multiple plugins per hook
   * - **Semantics**
     - Replaces the default implementation
     - Runs in addition to the default
   * - **Return value**
     - Used by the caller
     - None (fire-and-forget)
   * - **Typical use**
     - Custom download, build, or resolution logic
     - Publishing wheels, validation, logging

Per-Package Overrides
---------------------

An override module provides alternative implementations for specific
build steps.  Fromager looks up the module by the canonicalized package
name.  If the module defines the requested method, it is called instead
of the default; otherwise the default runs.

Override hooks cover resolution, source acquisition, building,
dependency extraction, and build environment customization.  Third-party
packages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``
entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to
a Python module.

The ``is_pre_built`` override is called after a version is selected. It
can return ``True`` or ``False`` to choose wheels or source distributions
for that version, or ``None`` to defer to version-specific and variant
settings. The bootstrapper then resolves the download URL for the
selected artifact type and wheel server.

See :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their
arguments.

Global Hooks
------------

Global hooks are event callbacks that fire for every package.  All
registered plugins for a hook are called sequentially.  They cannot
alter the build result — they are purely side-effecting notifications.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Hook
     - When it fires
   * - ``post_build``
     - After a wheel is built from source (not for prebuilt wheels)
   * - ``prebuilt_wheel``
     - After a prebuilt wheel is downloaded (not built from source)
   * - ``post_bootstrap``
     - After a package is bootstrapped, before its install dependencies
       are processed

Third-party packages register hooks via the ``fromager.hooks``
entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a hook name to
a callable.

See :doc:`/customization` for examples and argument details.

Package Settings
================

Fromager uses a layered settings system to configure how each package
is resolved, downloaded, patched, and built.  Settings flow from YAML
files on disk through a merge pipeline into a single facade object
used by the build pipeline.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`/reference/config-reference` documents every configuration
   field.  :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.

Settings Loading Flow
---------------------

.. code-block:: text

   CLI flags
   (--settings-file, --settings-dir, --patches-dir)
         │
         ▼
   Settings.from_files()
   ├── Load settings.yaml ──► SettingsFile (global config)
   └── Glob settings/*.yaml ──► PackageSettings (one per package)
         │
         ▼
   Settings object (held by WorkContext)
         │
         │  package_build_info("torch")  (on demand, cached)
         ▼
   PackageBuildInfo
   (single facade used by the build pipeline)

``PackageBuildInfo`` objects are created lazily the first time a
package is queried and cached for the rest of the run.

Version-specific ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url`` values under
``variants.<variant>.versions.<version>`` override the variant defaults.
After selecting a version, the bootstrapper resolves its download URL
again when these settings select a different artifact type or wheel
server. Local version suffixes are ignored when matching YAML version
keys, so ``2.8.0+cpu`` uses the settings for ``2.8.0``. If URL
re-resolution fails, the original URL is retained with a warning.

Directory Structure
-------------------

.. code-block:: text

   overrides/
   ├── settings.yaml              # Global settings
   ├── settings/                  # Per-package settings
   │   ├── torch.yaml
   │   ├── flash-attn.yaml
   │   └── ...
   └── patches/                   # Patches
       ├── torch/                 # Unversioned (all versions)
       │   ├── 001-fix.patch
       │   └── cpu/               # Variant-specific
       │       └── 002-cpu.patch
       └── torch-2.4.0/           # Version-specific
           └── 001-ver.patch

Package YAML filenames use the canonicalized package name (lowercase,
hyphens).  All three directories are configurable via CLI flags.

Merge Order
-----------

Settings are merged from least-specific to most-specific.  Later
layers override earlier ones:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  1. Pydantic field defaults                      │
   │     (empty env, default build options, etc.)     │
   │                                                  │
   │  2. Global settings.yaml                         │
   │     (SBOM config, global changelog)              │
   │                                                  │
   │  3. Per-package YAML file                        │
   │     (env, resolver, build options, patches, ...) │
   │                                                  │
   │  4. Variant overrides (within package YAML)      │
   │     (env vars, pre_built, wheel_server_url)      │
   │                                                  │
   │  5. Version-specific patches and changelog       │
   │     (patches/<pkg>-<version>/, changelog entries)│
   │                                                  │
   │  6. Override plugin hooks (runtime)              │
   │     (update_extra_environ can mutate env vars)   │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

For environment variables specifically, the merge order within a
single ``get_extra_environ()`` call is: parallel-jobs settings, build
environment paths, package-level ``env``, then variant-level ``env``.
Entries can reference earlier values using ``$VAR`` template syntax.

PackageBuildInfo Facade
-----------------------

``PackageBuildInfo`` is the single interface the build pipeline uses to
query all package configuration.  It wraps a ``PackageSettings`` and
adds variant awareness, patch discovery, and template resolution.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Category
     - What it provides
   * - **Identity**
     - Package name, variant, whether a config file exists, override
       plugin module
   * - **Resolution**
     - Sdist server URL, include wheels/sdists flags, platform
       filtering, per-package cooldown override
   * - **Build config**
     - Environment variables, parallel jobs, exclusive build flag,
       PEP 517 config settings, build directory
   * - **Source**
     - Download URL and filename templates with ``${version}``
       substitution, git submodule options
   * - **Patches**
     - Merged list of unversioned + version-specific + variant-specific
       patch files, sorted by filename
   * - **Metadata**
     - Build tag (from changelog length), annotations, PURL config,
       pyproject.toml overrides

See :doc:`/reference/config-reference` for the full field reference.

diff --git a/docs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst b/docs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst
index 43d5f28..fa6bdf8 100644
--- a/docs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst
+++ b/docs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst
@@ -53,6 +53,12 @@ packages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``
 entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to
 a Python module.
 
+The ``is_pre_built`` override is called after a version is selected. It
+can return ``True`` or ``False`` to choose wheels or source distributions
+for that version, or ``None`` to defer to version-specific and variant
+settings. The bootstrapper then resolves the download URL for the
+selected artifact type and wheel server.
+
 See :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their
 arguments.
 
diff --git a/docs/concepts/package-settings.rst b/docs/concepts/package-settings.rst
index 2f0a0d7..aa679f9 100644
--- a/docs/concepts/package-settings.rst
+++ b/docs/concepts/package-settings.rst
@@ -35,6 +35,14 @@ Settings Loading Flow
 ``PackageBuildInfo`` objects are created lazily the first time a
 package is queried and cached for the rest of the run.
 
+Version-specific ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url`` values under
+``variants.<variant>.versions.<version>`` override the variant defaults.
+After selecting a version, the bootstrapper resolves its download URL
+again when these settings select a different artifact type or wheel
+server. Local version suffixes are ignored when matching YAML version
+keys, so ``2.8.0+cpu`` uses the settings for ``2.8.0``. If URL
+re-resolution fails, the original URL is retained with a warning.
+
 Directory Structure
 -------------------

Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.\n---\n\n# Surgical patch\n\nReproduce failure first when economical; otherwise capture strongest available evidence.\n\n- Trace symptom to responsible mechanism.\n- Change narrowest layer that owns incorrect behavior.\n- Preserve unrelated behavior and user changes.\n- Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.\n- Add only regression proof relevant to task.\n\nRun focused proof plus nearest affected gate. Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\nCONTRIBUTING.md\nAGENTS.md\ntests/test_bootstrapper_iterative.py\ntests/test_packagesettings.py\nsrc/fromager/wheels.py\nsrc/fromager/packagesettings/_pbi.py\nsrc/fromager/packagesettings/_models.py\nsrc/fromager/bootstrapper/_start.py\ndocs/concepts/package-settings.rst\ndocs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Settings\n================\n\nFromager uses a layered settings system to configure how each package\nis resolved, downloaded, patched, and built.  Settings flow from YAML\nfiles on disk through a merge pipeline into a single facade object\nused by the build pipeline.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`/reference/config-reference` documents every configuration\n   field.  :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n\nSettings Loading Flow\n---------------------\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   CLI flags\n   (--settings-file, --settings-dir, --patches-dir)\n         │\n         ▼\n   Settings.from_files()\n   ├── Load settings.yaml ──► SettingsFile (global config)\n   └── Glob settings/*.yaml ──► PackageSettings (one per package)\n         │\n         ▼\n   Settings object (held by WorkContext)\n         │\n         │  package_build_info(\"torch\")  (on demand, cached)\n         ▼\n   PackageBuildInfo\n   (single facade used by the build pipeline)\n\n``PackageBuildInfo`` objects are created lazily the first time a\npackage is queried and cached for the rest of the run.\n\nDirectory Structure\n-------------------\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   overrides/\n   ├── settings.yaml              # Global settings\n   ├── settings/                  # Per-package settings\n   │   ├── torch.yaml\n   │   ├── flash-attn.yaml\n   │   └── ...\n   └── patches/                   # Patches\n       ├── torch/                 # Unversioned (all versions)\n       │   ├── 001-fix.patch\n       │   └── cpu/               # Variant-specific\n       │       └── 002-cpu.patch\n       └── torch-2.4.0/           # Version-specific\n           └── 001-ver.patch\n\nPackage YAML filenames use the canonicalized package name (lowercase,\nhyphens).  All three directories are configurable via CLI flags.\n\nMerge Order\n-----------\n\nSettings are merged from least-specific to most-specific.  Later\nlayers override earlier ones:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │  1. Pydantic field defaults                      │\n   │     (empty env, default build options, etc.)     │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  2. Global settings.yaml                         │\n   │     (SBOM config, global changelog)              │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  3. Per-package YAML file                        │\n   │     (env, resolver, build options, patches, ...) │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  4. Variant overrides (within package YAML)      │\n   │     (env vars, pre_built, wheel_server_url)      │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  5. Version-specific patches and changelog       │\n   │     (patches/<pkg>-<version>/, changelog entries)│\n   │                                                  │\n   │  6. Override plugin hooks (runtime)              │\n   │     (update_extra_environ can mutate env vars)   │\n   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\nFor environment variables specifically, the merge order within a\nsingle ``get_extra_environ()`` call is: parallel-jobs settings, build\nenvironment paths, package-level ``env``, then variant-level ``env``.\nEntries can reference earlier values using ``$VAR`` template syntax.\n\nPackageBuildInfo Facade\n-----------------------\n\n``PackageBuildInfo`` is the single interface the build pipeline uses to\nquery all package configuration.  It wraps a ``PackageSettings`` and\nadds variant awareness, patch discovery, and template resolution.\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Category\n     - What it provides\n   * - **Identity**\n     - Package name, variant, whether a config file exists, override\n       plugin module\n   * - **Resolution**\n     - Sdist server URL, include wheels/sdists flags, platform\n       filtering, per-package cooldown override\n   * - **Build config**\n     - Environment variables, parallel jobs, exclusive build flag,\n       PEP 517 config settings, build directory\n   * - **Source**\n     - Download URL and filename templates with ``${version}``\n       substitution, git submodule options\n   * - **Patches**\n     - Merged list of unversioned + version-specific + variant-specific\n       patch files, sorted by filename\n   * - **Metadata**\n     - Build tag (from changelog length), annotations, PURL config,\n       pyproject.toml overrides\n\nSee :doc:`/reference/config-reference` for the full field reference.\nHooks and Overrides\n===================\n\nFromager has two plugin systems that serve different purposes:\n**per-package overrides** replace default behavior for a specific\npackage, while **global hooks** broadcast notifications after events\nfor every package.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n   :doc:`/reference/hooks` documents each override hook's arguments and\n   return values.  :doc:`/customization` covers global hooks with code\n   examples.\n\nComparison\n----------\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 20 40 40\n\n   * - Aspect\n     - Per-Package Overrides\n     - Global Hooks\n   * - **Scope**\n     - One named package\n     - Every package\n   * - **Cardinality**\n     - At most one override module per package\n     - Multiple plugins per hook\n   * - **Semantics**\n     - Replaces the default implementation\n     - Runs in addition to the default\n   * - **Return value**\n     - Used by the caller\n     - None (fire-and-forget)\n   * - **Typical use**\n     - Custom download, build, or resolution logic\n     - Publishing wheels, validation, logging\n\nPer-Package Overrides\n---------------------\n\nAn override module provides alternative implementations for specific\nbuild steps.  Fromager looks up the module by the canonicalized package\nname.  If the module defines the requested method, it is called instead\nof the default; otherwise the default runs.\n\nOverride hooks cover resolution, source acquisition, building,\ndependency extraction, and build environment customization.  Third-party\npackages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``\nentry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to\na Python module.\n\nSee :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their\narguments.\n\nGlobal Hooks\n------------\n\nGlobal hooks are event callbacks that fire for every package.  All\nregistered plugins for a hook are called sequentially.  They cannot\nalter the build result — they are purely side-effecting notifications.\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Hook\n     - When it fires\n   * - ``post_build``\n     - After a wheel is built from source (not for prebuilt wheels)\n   * - ``prebuilt_wheel``\n     - After a prebuilt wheel is downloaded (not built from source)\n   * - ``post_bootstrap``\n     - After a package is bootstrapped, before its install dependencies\n       are processed\n\nThird-party packages register hooks via the ``fromager.hooks``\nentry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a hook name to\na callable.\n\nSee :doc:`/customization` for examples and argument details.\n","exit_code":1,"status":"failed"}}

In\n        ``multiple_versions`` mode, processes all matching versions per requirement.\n\n        Args:\n            requirements: Top-level requirements to resolve and bootstrap.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Resolve all top-level reqs and build initial stack.\n        # Use the token pattern (no try/finally) so that if resolution raises\n        # in normal mode, the context var stays set for the top-level error\n        # handler in __main__.py to include the package name in its log message.\n        stack: list[Phase] = []\n        initial_items: list[Phase] = []\n        for req in requirements:\n            token = requirement_ctxvar.set(req)\n            result = self._resolve_and_add_top_level(req)\n            requirement_ctxvar.reset(token)\n            if result is not None:\n                initial_items.append(\n                    Resolve(\n                        WorkItem(\n                            req=req,\n                            req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n                            why_snapshot=[],\n                            parent=None,\n                        )\n                    )\n                )\n        self._push_items(stack, initial_items)\n\n        self._run_bootstrap_loop(stack)\n\n    def _run_bootstrap_loop(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Run the iterative DFS bootstrap loop over a pre-built work stack.\n\n        Pops items one at a time, dispatches each phase, and pushes any\n        follow-on items (continuations and new dependencies) back onto the\n        stack. Updates the progress bar as items complete.\n\n        Args:\n            stack: Initial list of ``Phase`` objects to process. Modified\n                in-place; empty on return.\n        \"\"\"\n        while stack:\n            self._record_stack_state(stack)\n            item = stack.pop()\n            self.why = list(item.work_item.why_snapshot)\n\n            with (\n                req_ctxvar_context(item.work_item.req, item.work_item.resolved_version),\n                self._track_why(item),\n            ):\n                if item.requires_exclusive_run:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s requires exclusive build, draining background pool\",\n                        item.work_item.req,\n                    )\n                    self._drain_background_pool()\n                try:\n                    new_items = item.run(self)\n                except Exception as err:\n                    new_items = self._handle_phase_error(item, err)\n\n            new_dep_count = sum(1 for it in new_items if isinstance(it, Resolve))\n            if new_dep_count > 0:\n                self.progressbar.update_total(new_dep_count)\n            if not new_items:\n                self.progressbar.update()\n\n            self._push_items(stack, new_items)\n\n    def _bootstrap_one(self, req: Requirement, req_type: RequirementType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap a single requirement using an iterative DFS loop.\n\n        Internal method used only by the git URL resolution path\n        (``_handle_build_requirements``). All other callers should use\n        ``bootstrap(requirements)`` instead.\n\n        Uses an explicit LIFO stack instead of recursion to handle arbitrarily\n        deep dependency graphs without hitting Python's recursion limit.\n\n        In test mode, catches build exceptions, records package name, and continues.\n        In normal mode, raises exceptions immediately (fail-fast).\n\n        When multiple_versions is enabled, bootstraps all matching versions instead\n        of just the highest version.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(f\"bootstrapping {req} as {req_type} dependency of {self.why[-1:]}\")\n\n        # Capture parent from current why stack before creating work items\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None\n        if self.why:\n            _, parent_req, parent_version = self.why[-1]\n            parent = (parent_req, parent_version)\n\n        # Save the why stack so we can restore it after the iterative loop\n        # (the loop modifies self.why for each work item)\n        saved_why = list(self.why)\n\n        # Single RESOLVE item — resolution, version expansion, and error\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport collections\nimport dataclasses\nimport graphlib\nimport json\nimport logging\nimport pathlib\nimport threading\nimport typing\n\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom .read import open_file_or_url\nfrom .requirements_file import RequirementType\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from .context import WorkContext\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nROOT = \"\"\n\n\nclass DependencyEdgeDict(typing.TypedDict):\n    req_type: str\n    req: str\n    key: str\n\n\nclass DependencyNodeDict(typing.TypedDict):\n    download_url: str\n    canonicalized_name: str\n    version: str\n    pre_built: bool\n    # not set in older graph files\n    constraint: typing.NotRequired[str | None]\n    edges: list[DependencyEdgeDict]\n\n\n@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True)\nclass DependencyNode:\n    canonicalized_name: NormalizedName\n    version: Version\n    download_url: str = dataclasses.field(default=\"\", compare=False)\n    pre_built: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)\n    constraint: Requirement | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)\n    # additional fields\n    key: str = dataclasses.field(init=False, compare=False, repr=False)\n    parents: list[DependencyEdge] = dataclasses.field(\n        default_factory=list,\n        init=False,\n        compare=False,\n        repr=False,\n    )\n    children: list[DependencyEdge] = dataclasses.field(\n        default_factory=list,\n        init=False,\n        compare=False,\n        repr=False,\n    )\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.canonicalized_name == ROOT:\n            # root has a special key\n            object.__setattr__(self, \"key\", ROOT)\n        else:\n            object.__setattr__(\n                self, \"key\", f\"{self.canonicalized_name}=={self.version}\"\n            )\n\n    @property\n    def requirement(self) -> Requirement:\n        if self.canonicalized_name == ROOT:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"root node is not a requirement\")\n        return Requirement(self.key)\n\n    def add_child(\n        self,\n        child: DependencyNode,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n    ) -> None:\n        current_to_child_edge = DependencyEdge(\n            req=req, req_type=req_type, destination_node=child\n        )\n        self.children.append(current_to_child_edge)\n        child_to_current_edge = DependencyEdge(\n            req=req, req_type=req_type, destination_node=self\n        )\n        # will create a cyclic dependency in memory, which will make it harder to garbage collect\n        # not an issue for fromager since it is used as a short-lived process\n        child.parents.append(child_to_current_edge)\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> DependencyNodeDict:\n        return {\n            \"download_url\": self.download_url,\n            \"pre_built\": self.pre_built,\n            \"version\": str(self.version),\n            \"canonicalized_name\": str(self.canonicalized_name),\n            \"constraint\": str(self.constraint) if self.constraint else None,\n            \"edges\": [edge.to_dict() for edge in self.children],\n        }\n\n    def get_incoming_install_edges(self) -> list[DependencyEdge]:\n        return [\n            edge for edge in self.parents if edge.req_type == RequirementType.INSTALL\n        ]\n\n    def get_outgoing_edges(\n        self, req_name: str, req_type: RequirementType\n    ) -> list[DependencyEdge]:\n        return [\n            edge\n            for edge in self.children\n            if canonicalize_name(edge.req.name) == canonicalize_name(req_name)\n            and edge.req_type == req_type\n        ]\n\n    @classmethod\n    def construct_root_node(cls) -> DependencyNode:\n        return cls(\n            canonicalize_name(ROOT),\n            # version doesn't really matter for root\n            Version(\"0\"),\n        )\n\n    def iter_build_requirements(self) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyNode]:\n        \"\"\"Get all unique, recursive build requirements\n\n        Yield all direct and indirect requirements to build the dependency.\n        Includes direct build dependencies and their recursive **install**\n        requirements.\n\n        The result is equivalent to the set of ``[build-system].requires``\n        plus all ``Requires-Dist`` of build system requirements -- all\n        packages in the build environment.\n        \"\"\"\n        visited: set[str] = set()\n        # The outer loop iterates over all children and picks\n        # direct build requirements. For each build requirement, it traverses\n        # all children and recursively get their install requirements\n        # (depth first).\n        for edge in self.children:\n            if edge.key in visited:\n                # optimization: don't traverse visited nodes\n                continue\n            if not edge.req_type.is_build_requirement:\n                # not a build requirement\n                continue\n            visited.add(edge.key)\n            # it's a new ``[build-system].requires``.\n            yield edge.destination_node\n            # recursively get install dependencies of this build dep (depth first).\n            for install_edge in self._traverse_install_requirements(\n                edge.destination_node.children, visited\n            ):\n                yield install_edge.destination_node\n\n    def iter_all_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyNode]:\n        \"\"\"Get all unique, recursive dependencies following every edge type.\n\n        Yields every reachable node exactly once using iterative DFS.\n        Follows install, build, and toplevel edges.\n        \"\"\"\n        visited: set[str] = {self.key}\n        stack: list[DependencyNode] = [self]\n        while stack:\n            current = stack.pop()\n            for edge in current.children:\n                child_node = edge.destination_node\n                if child_node.key in visited:\n                    continue\n                visited.add(child_node.key)\n                yield child_node\n                stack.append(child_node)\n\n    def iter_install_requirements(self) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyNode]:\n        \"\"\"Get all unique, recursive install requirements\"\"\"\n        visited: set[str] = set()\n        for edge in self._traverse_install_requirements(self.children, visited):\n            yield edge.destination_node\n\n    def _traverse_install_requirements(\n        self,\n        start_edges: list[DependencyEdge],\n        visited: set[str],\n    ) -> typing.Iterable[DependencyEdge]:\n        # Depth-first walk of install requirement edges, skipping nodes\n        # already visited to avoid loops in the dependency graph.\n        for edge in start_edges:\n            if edge.key in visited:\n                continue\n            if not edge.req_type.is_install_requirement:\n                continue\n            visited.add(edge.destination_node.key)\n            yield edge\n            yield from self._traverse_install_requirements(\n                edge.destination_node.children, visited\n            )\n\n\n@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True)\nclass DependencyEdge:\n    key: str = dataclasses.field(init=False, repr=True, compare=True)\n    destination_node: DependencyNode = dataclasses.field(repr=False, compare=False)\n    req: Requirement = dataclasses.field(repr=True, compare=True)\n    req_type: RequirementType = dataclasses.field(repr=True, compare=True)\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        object.__setattr__(self, \"key\", self.destination_node.key)\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> DependencyEdgeDict:\n        return {\n            \"key\": self.key,\n            \"req_type\": str(self.req_type),\n            \"req\": str(self.req),\n        }\n\n\nclass DependencyGraph:\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.nodes: dict[str, DependencyNode] = {}\n        self.clear()\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_file(\n        cls,\n        graph_file: pathlib.Path | str,\n    ) -> DependencyGraph:\n        with open_file_or_url(graph_file) as f:\n            # TODO: add JSON validation to ensure it is a parsable graph json\n            raw_graph = typing.cast(dict[str, dict], json.load(f))\n            return cls.from_dict(raw_graph)\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_dict(\n        cls,\n\"\"\"SettingsFile and Settings classes.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport pathlib\nimport typing\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\n\nimport pydantic\nimport yaml\nfrom packaging.utils import canonicalize_name\nfrom pydantic import Field\n\nfrom .. import overrides\nfrom ._models import ExternalCommands, PackageSettings, SbomSettings\nfrom ._pbi import PackageBuildInfo\nfrom ._typedefs import MODEL_CONFIG, GlobalChangelog, Package, Variant\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass SettingsFile(pydantic.BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Models global settings file `settings.yaml`\n\n    ::\n\n      changelog:\n        cuda:\n          - \"2024-09-13: updated CUDA version\"\n        rocm:\n          - \"2024-09-01: updated ROCm version\"\n    \"\"\"\n\n    model_config = MODEL_CONFIG\n\n    changelog: GlobalChangelog = Field(default_factory=dict)\n    \"\"\"Changelog entries\"\"\"\n\n    sbom: SbomSettings | None = None\n    \"\"\"SBOM generation settings\n\n    When set, Fromager generates SPDX 2.3 SBOM documents and embeds\n    them in built wheels per PEP 770. When absent (default), no SBOMs\n    are generated.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    external_commands: ExternalCommands = Field(default_factory=ExternalCommands)\n    \"\"\"Environment variable filtering for subprocesses\n\n    Controls which environment variables are passed to child processes\n    using ``keep_env`` / ``delete_env`` patterns.  Defaults to no\n    filtering.\n\n    .. versionadded:: 0.92.0\n    \"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_string(\n        cls,\n        raw_yaml: str,\n        *,\n        source: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,\n    ) -> SettingsFile:\n        \"\"\"Load from raw yaml string\"\"\"\n        parsed: typing.Any = yaml.safe_load(raw_yaml)\n        if parsed is None:\n            # empty file\n            parsed = {}\n        elif not isinstance(parsed, Mapping):\n            raise TypeError(f\"invalid yaml, not a dict (source: {source!r}): {parsed}\")\n        # ignore legacy settings\n        parsed.pop(\"pre_built\", None)\n        parsed.pop(\"packages\", None)\n        # Ensure changelog is correct type\n        if \"changelog\" in parsed and not isinstance(parsed[\"changelog\"], dict):\n            parsed[\"changelog\"] = {}\n        try:\n            return cls(**parsed)\n        except Exception as err:\n            raise RuntimeError(\n                f\"failed to load global settings (source: {source!r}): {err}\"\n            ) from err\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_file(cls, filename: pathlib.Path) -> SettingsFile:\n        \"\"\"Load from file\n\n        Raises :exc:`FileNotFound` when the file is not found.\n        The package name is taken from the stem of the file name.\n        \"\"\"\n        filename = filename.absolute()\n        logger.info(\"loading settings from %s\", filename)\n        raw_yaml = filename.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        return cls.from_string(raw_yaml, source=filename)\n\n\nclass Settings:\n    \"\"\"Settings interface for settings file and package settings\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        settings: SettingsFile,\n        package_settings: typing.Iterable[PackageSettings],\n        variant: Variant | str,\n        patches_dir: pathlib.Path,\n        max_jobs: int | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._settings = settings\n        self._package_settings: dict[Package, PackageSettings] = {\n            p.name: p for p in package_settings\n        }\n        self._variant = typing.cast(Variant, variant)\n        self._patches_dir = patches_dir\n        self._max_jobs = max_jobs\n        self._pbi_cache: dict[Package, PackageBuildInfo] = {}\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_files(\n        cls,\n        *,\n        settings_file: pathlib.Path,\n        settings_dir: pathlib.Path,\n        variant: Variant | str,\n        patches_dir: pathlib.Path,\n        max_jobs: int | None,\n    ) -> Settings:\n        \"\"\"Create Settings from settings.yaml and directory\"\"\"\n        if settings_file.is_file():\n            settings = SettingsFile.from_file(settings_file)\n        else:\n            logger.debug(\n                \"settings file %s does not exist, ignoring\", settings_file.absolute()\n            )\n            settings = SettingsFile()\n        package_settings = [\n            PackageSettings.from_file(package_file)\n            for package_file in sorted(settings_dir.glob(\"*.yaml\"))\n        ]\n        return cls(\n            settings=settings,\n            package_settings=package_settings,\n            variant=variant,\n            patches_dir=patches_dir,\n            max_jobs=max_jobs,\n        )\n\n    @property\n    def variant(self) -> Variant:\n        \"\"\"Get current variant\"\"\"\n        return self._variant\n\n    @variant.setter\n    def variant(self, v: Variant) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Change current variant (for testing)\"\"\"\n        # reset cache\n        self._pbi_cache.clear()\n        self._variant = v\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
