Must be\n        called after resolution but before the seen-check so that every edge\n        is captured even for packages that are not built again.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added.\n            req_type: Whether this is a build-system, build-backend, install,\n                or other dependency kind.\n            req_version: The resolved version of ``req``.\n            download_url: Source URL used to obtain the distribution.\n            parent: ``(req, version)`` of the package that introduced ``req``,\n                or ``None`` for top-level requirements.\n        \"\"\"\n        parent_req, parent_version = parent if parent else (None, None)\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        # Update the dependency graph after we determine that this requirement is\n        # useful but before we determine if it is redundant so that we capture all\n        # edges to use for building a valid constraints file.\n        self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(\n            parent_name=canonicalize_name(parent_req.name) if parent_req else None,\n            parent_version=parent_version,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            req=req,\n            req_version=req_version,\n            download_url=download_url,\n            pre_built=pbi.is_pre_built(req_version),\n            constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),\n        )\n        self._write_graph_async()\n\n    def _sort_requirements(\n        self,\n        requirements: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n    ) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:\n        return sorted(requirements, key=operator.attrgetter(\"name\"))\n\n    def _resolved_key(\n        self, req: Requirement, version: Version, typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"]\n    ) -> SeenKey:\n        return (\n            canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            tuple(sorted(req.extras)),\n            str(version),\n            typ,\n        )\n\n    def mark_as_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Track sdist and wheel builds\n\n        A sdist-only build just contains as an sdist.\n        A wheel build counts as wheel and sdist, because the presence of a\n        either implies we have built a wheel from an sdist or we have a\n        prebuilt wheel that will never have an sdist.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Mark sdist seen for sdist-only build and wheel build\n        self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"sdist\"))\n        if not sdist_only:\n            # Mark wheel seen only for wheel build\n            self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"wheel\"))\n\n    def has_been_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if this requirement/version has already been processed.\n\n        Uses the same sdist-vs-wheel distinction as ``mark_as_seen``:\n        when ``sdist_only`` is True, checks only for a prior sdist build;\n        otherwise checks for a prior wheel build.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement to check.\n            version: The resolved version to check.\n            sdist_only: If True, check for a sdist-only build instead of a\n                full wheel build.\n        \"\"\"\n        typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"] = \"sdist\" if sdist_only else \"wheel\"\n        return self._resolved_key(req, version, typ) in self._seen_requirements\n\n    def add_to_build_order(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n        source_type: SourceType,\n        prebuilt: bool = False,\n        constraint: Requirement | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a package to the build-order list if not already present.\n\n        Deduplicates by ``(canonicalized_name, version)`` so the same package\n        cls,\n        graph_dict: dict[str, dict[str, typing.Any]],\n    ) -> DependencyGraph:\n        graph = cls()\n        # Stack-based DFS to reconstruct graph from serialized dict,\n        # skipping nodes already visited to avoid processing shared\n        # dependencies twice.\n        stack = [ROOT]\n        visited = set()\n        while stack:\n            curr_key = stack.pop()\n            if curr_key in visited:\n                continue\n            node_dict = typing.cast(DependencyNodeDict, graph_dict[curr_key])\n            parent_name = parent_version = None\n            if curr_key != ROOT:\n                parent_name = canonicalize_name(node_dict[\"canonicalized_name\"])\n                parent_version = Version(node_dict[\"version\"])\n            for raw_edge in node_dict[\"edges\"]:\n                edge_dict = typing.cast(DependencyEdgeDict, raw_edge)\n                destination_node_dict = typing.cast(\n                    DependencyNodeDict, graph_dict[edge_dict[\"key\"]]\n                )\n                constraint_value: str | None = destination_node_dict.get(\"constraint\")\n                constraint: Requirement | None = (\n                    Requirement(constraint_value) if constraint_value else None\n                )\n                graph.add_dependency(\n                    parent_name=parent_name,\n                    parent_version=parent_version,\n                    req_type=RequirementType(edge_dict[\"req_type\"]),\n                    req=Requirement(edge_dict[\"req\"]),\n                    req_version=Version(destination_node_dict[\"version\"]),\n                    download_url=destination_node_dict[\"download_url\"],\n                    pre_built=destination_node_dict[\"pre_built\"],\n                    constraint=constraint,\n                )\n                stack.append(edge_dict[\"key\"])\n            visited.add(curr_key)\n        return graph\n\n    def clear(self) -> None:\n        self.nodes.clear()\n        self.nodes[ROOT] = DependencyNode.construct_root_node()\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        # exclude ROOT\n        return len(self.nodes) - 1\n\n    def _to_dict(self) -> dict[str, typing.Any]:\n        raw_graph = {}\n        stack = [self.nodes[ROOT]]\n        visited = set()\n        while stack:\n            node = stack.pop()\n            raw_graph[node.key] = node.to_dict()\n            for child in node.children:\n                if child.destination_node.key not in visited:\n                    stack.append(child.destination_node)\n            visited.add(node.key)\n        return raw_graph\n\n    def serialize(self, file_handle: typing.TextIO) -> None:\n        raw_graph = self._to_dict()\n        json.dump(raw_graph, file_handle, indent=2, default=str)\n\n    def _add_node(\n        self,\n        req_name: NormalizedName,\n        version: Version,\n        download_url: str,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        constraint: Requirement | None,\n    ) -> DependencyNode:\n        new_node = DependencyNode(\n            canonicalized_name=req_name,\n            version=version,\n            download_url=download_url,\n            pre_built=pre_built,\n            constraint=constraint,\n        )\n        # check if a node with that key already exists. if it does then use that\n        node = self.nodes.get(new_node.key, new_node)\n        # store the node in case we are using new_node\n        self.nodes[node.key] = node\n        return node\n\n    def add_dependency(\n        self,\n        parent_name: NormalizedName | None,\n        parent_version: Version | None,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_version: Version,\n        download_url: str = \"\",\n        pre_built: bool = False,\n        constraint: Requirement | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        logger.debug(\n            \"recording %s dependency %s%s -> %s==%s\",\n            req_type,\n            parent_name if parent_name else f\"({RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL})\",\n            f\"=={parent_version}\" if parent_version else \"\",\n            req.name,\n            req_version,\n        )\n\n        node = self._add_node(\n            req_name=canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            version=req_version,\n            download_url=download_url,\n            pre_built=pre_built,\n            constraint=constraint,\n        )\n\n        parent_key = ROOT if parent_name is None else f\"{parent_name}=={parent_version}\"\n        if parent_key not in self.nodes:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Trying to add {node.key} to parent {parent_key} but {parent_key} does not exist\"\n            )\n\n        self.nodes[parent_key].add_child(node, req=req, req_type=req_type)\n\n    def remove_dependency(\n        self,\n        req_name: NormalizedName,\n        req_version: Version,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Remove a dependency node and any orphaned descendants from the graph.\n\n        Removes the node and all edges pointing to it. Child nodes that have\n        no remaining parents after removal are iteratively removed as well.\n\n        Args:\n            req_name: Canonical name of the package\n            req_version: Version of the package\n        \"\"\"\n        key = f\"{req_name}=={req_version}\"\n        if key not in self.nodes:\n            logger.debug(f\"Cannot remove {key} - not in graph\")\n            return\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import logging
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start, _re_resolve_url
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)


class TestPhaseClassVariables:
    """Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "cls, expected_phase, expected_tracks_why",
        [
            (Resolve, BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE, False),
            (Start, BootstrapPhase.START, False),
            (PrepareSource, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE, True),
            (PrepareBuild, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD, True),
            (Build, BootstrapPhase.BUILD, True),
            (ProcessInstallDeps, BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS, True),
            (Complete, BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE, True),
        ],
    )

class Cart:
    def __init__(self, tax_rate=0.0):
        self.items = []
        self.tax_rate = tax_rate

    def add(self, price, qty=1):
        self.items.append((price, qty))

    def total(self):
        return compute_total(self.items, self.tax_rate)

def compute_total(items, tax_rate=0.0):
    """Return the total price of items with tax applied.

    items: iterable of (unit_price, quantity)
    """
    subtotal = sum(price * qty for price, qty in items)
    return round(subtotal * (1 + tax_rate), 2)

Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6.     assert cfg == {
        "server": {"host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 8080, "debug": False},

import math
from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence


def distance(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])


def perimeter(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    if len(points) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return sum(distance(points[i], points[(i + 1) % len(points)]) for i in range(len(points)))


def centroid(points: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    if not points:
        return None
    n = len(points)
    return (sum(p[0] for p in points) / n, sum(p[1] for p in points) / n)


class Polygon:
    def __init__(self, points: Iterable[Sequence[float]], name: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.points = list(points)
        self.name = name

    def area(self) -> float:
        s = 0.0
        for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(self.points):
            x2, y2 = self.points[(i + 1) % len(self.points)]
            s += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
        return abs(s) / 2

    def scaled(self, factor: float) -> Polygon:
        return Polygon([(x * factor, y * factor) for x, y in self.points], self.name)

    def describe(self) -> dict[str, str | int | float | None]:
        return {"name": self.name, "sides": len(self.points), "area": self.area()}

Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_9","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,260p' geo/shapes.py\"","aggregated_output":"import math\n\n\ndef distance(a, b):\n    return math.hypot(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])\n\n\ndef perimeter(points):\n    if len(points) < 2:\n        return 0.0\n    return sum(distance(points[i], points[(i + 1) % len(points)]) for i in range(len(points)))\n\n\ndef centroid(points):\n    if not points:\n        return None\n    n = len(points)\n    return (sum(p[0] for p in points) / n, sum(p[1] for p in points) / n)\n\n\nclass Polygon:\n    def __init__(self, points, name=None):\n        self.points = list(points)\n        self.name = name\n\n    def area(self):\n        s = 0.0\n        for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(self.points):\n            x2, y2 = self.points[(i + 1) % len(self.points)]\n            s += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1\n        return abs(s) / 2\n\n    def scaled(self, factor):\n        return Polygon([(x * factor, y * factor) for x, y in self.points], self.name)\n\n    def describe(self):\n        return {\"name\": self.name, \"sides\": len(self.points), \"area\": self.area()}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

import time
from collections import OrderedDict


class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity, ttl=None, clock=time.monotonic):
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be greater than zero")

        self.capacity = capacity
        self.ttl = ttl
        self._clock = clock
        self._items = OrderedDict()
        self._expirations = OrderedDict()
        self._hits = 0
        self._misses = 0
        self._evictions = 0
        self._expiration_count = 0

    def _purge_expired(self, now=None):
        if self.ttl is None:
            return
        if now is None:
            now = self._clock()

        while self._expirations:
            key, expires_at = next(iter(self._expirations.items()))
            if expires_at > now:
                break

            self._expirations.popitem(last=False)
            item = self._items.get(key)
            if item is not None and item[1] == expires_at:
                del self._items[key]
                self._expiration_count += 1

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        self._purge_expired()
        try:
            value, _ = self._items[key]
        except KeyError:
            self._misses += 1
            return default

        self._items.move_to_end(key)
        self._hits += 1
        return value

    def put(self, key, value):
        now = self._clock() if self.ttl is not None else None
        self._purge_expired(now)

        expires_at = now + self.ttl if self.ttl is not None else None
        self._expirations.pop(key, None)
        self._items[key] = (value, expires_at)
        self._items.move_to_end(key)

        if expires_at is not None:
            self._expirations[key] = expires_at
            self._purge_expired(now)

        while len(self._items) > self.capacity:
            evicted_key, _ = self._items.popitem(last=False)
            self._expirations.pop(evicted_key, None)
            self._evictions += 1

    def delete(self, key):
        self._purge_expired()
        try:
            del self._items[key]
        except KeyError:
            return False

        self._expirations.pop(key, None)
        return True

    def stats(self):
        self._purge_expired()
        return {
            "hits": self._hits,
            "misses": self._misses,
            "evictions": self._evictions,
            "expirations": self._expiration_count,
        }

    def __len__(self):
        self._purge_expired()
        return len(self._items)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        self._purge_expired()
        return key in self._items

+import unittest
+
+from cachelib import LRUCache

+

+

+class LRUCacheTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_get_and_update_refresh_recency(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(2)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+
+        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("c"), 3)

+            "hits": 3,
+            "misses": 0,
+            "evictions": 1,
+            "expirations": 0,
+        })
+
+        cache.put("a", 10)
+        cache.put("d", 4)
+        self.assertNotIn("c", cache)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 10)
+
+    def test_contains_does_not_refresh_recency(self):
+        cache = LRUCache(2)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+
+        self.assertIn("a", cache)
+        cache.put("c", 3)
+
+        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
+        self.assertIn("b", cache)
+
+    def test_expired_get_counts_miss_and_expiration(self):
+        clock = FakeClock()
+        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=5, clock=clock)
+        cache.put("a", "value")
+
+        clock.now = 5
+        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a", "missing"), "missing")
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), {
+            "hits": 0,
+            "misses": 1,
+            "evictions": 0,
+            "expirations": 1,
+        })
+
+    def test_length_and_stats_purge_all_expired_entries(self):
+        clock = FakeClock()
+        cache = LRUCache(3, ttl=2, clock=clock)
+        cache.put("a", 1)
+        cache.put("b", 2)
+
+        clock.now = 2
+        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 0)
+        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 2)
+

import unittest

from cachelib import LRUCache


class FakeClock:
    def __init__(self, now=0.0):
        self.now = now

    def __call__(self):
        return self.now


class LRUCacheTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_get_and_update_refresh_recency(self):
        cache = LRUCache(2)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        cache.put("b", 2)

        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        cache.put("c", 3)

        self.assertNotIn("b", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 1)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("c"), 3)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), {
            "hits": 3,
            "misses": 0,
            "evictions": 1,
            "expirations": 0,
        })

        cache.put("a", 10)
        cache.put("d", 4)
        self.assertNotIn("c", cache)
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a"), 10)

    def test_contains_does_not_refresh_recency(self):
        cache = LRUCache(2)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        cache.put("b", 2)

        self.assertIn("a", cache)
        cache.put("c", 3)

        self.assertNotIn("a", cache)
        self.assertIn("b", cache)

    def test_expired_get_counts_miss_and_expiration(self):
        clock = FakeClock()
        cache = LRUCache(2, ttl=5, clock=clock)
        cache.put("a", "value")

        clock.now = 5
        self.assertEqual(cache.get("a", "missing"), "missing")
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), {
            "hits": 0,
            "misses": 1,
            "evictions": 0,
            "expirations": 1,
        })

    def test_length_and_stats_purge_all_expired_entries(self):
        clock = FakeClock()
        cache = LRUCache(3, ttl=2, clock=clock)
        cache.put("a", 1)
        cache.put("b", 2)

        clock.now = 2
        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 0)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats()["expirations"], 2)

    def test_delete_and_default_stats(self):
        cache = LRUCache(1)
        self.assertEqual(cache.stats(), {
            "hits": 0,
            "misses": 0,
            "evictions": 0,
            "expirations": 0,
        })
        cache.put("a", None)
        self.assertTrue(cache.delete("a"))
        self.assertFalse(cache.delete("a"))
        self.assertEqual(len(cache), 0)

    def test_nonpositive_capacity_is_rejected(self):
        for capacity in (0, -1):
            with self.subTest(capacity=capacity):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    LRUCache(capacity)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import argparse
import json
import sys


def count(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    return {"lines": text.count("\n"), "words": len(text.split()), "chars": len(text)}


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wc")
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    total = {"lines": 0, "words": 0, "chars": 0}
    files = []
    rc = 0
    for path in args.files:
        try:
            c = count(path)
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"wc: {path}: {e.strerror}", file=sys.stderr)
            rc = 1
            continue
        if args.json:
            files.append({"path": path, **c})
        else:
            print(f"{c['lines']:>8}{c['words']:>8}{c['chars']:>8} {path}")
        for k in total:
            total[k] += c[k]
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"files": files, "total": total}))
    elif len(args.files) > 1:
        print(f"{total['lines']:>8}{total['words']:>8}{total['chars']:>8} total")
    return rc

Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. import json

from wc.cli import main


def test_text(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    assert main([str(p)]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == f"       2       3      16 {p}\n"


def test_text_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"
    assert main([str(p), str(missing)]) == 1
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert captured.out == f"       2       3      16 {p}\n       2       3      16 total\n"
    assert captured.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"


def test_json(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    assert main(["--json", str(p)]) == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert captured.err == ""
    assert json.loads(captured.out) == {
        "files": [{"path": str(p), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16}],
        "total": {"lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
    }


def test_json_missing_file(tmp_path, capsys):
    p = tmp_path / "a.txt"; p.write_text("hello world\nbye\n")
    missing = tmp_path / "missing.txt"
    assert main(["--json", str(p), str(missing)]) == 1
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert json.loads(captured.out) == {
        "files": [{"path": str(p), "lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16}],
        "total": {"lines": 2, "words": 3, "chars": 16},
    }
    assert captured.err == f"wc: {missing}: No such file or directory\n"

"""Parse access log lines and summarize their records."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import math
from typing import Iterable


@dataclass
class Record:
    ts: datetime
    method: str
    path: str
    status: int
    latency_ms: float
    bytes: int


@dataclass
class Summary:
    total: int
    malformed: int
    by_status: dict[int, int]
    by_method: dict[str, int]
    p50_latency_ms: float
    p95_latency_ms: float
    bytes_total: int
    error_rate: float
    top_paths: list[tuple[str, int]]


def parse_line(line: str) -> Record | None:
    """Return a parsed record, or ``None`` when the line is malformed."""
    if not isinstance(line, str):
        return None

    fields = line.split()
    if len(fields) not in (5, 6):
        return None

    timestamp, method, path, status_text, latency_text = fields[:5]
    bytes_text = fields[5] if len(fields) == 6 else "0"

    try:
        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if ts.tzinfo is None or ts.utcoffset() is None:
            return None
        ts = ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)

        if not status_text.lstrip("+-").isdigit():
            return None
        if not bytes_text.lstrip("+-").isdigit():
            return None
        status = int(status_text)
        byte_count = int(bytes_text)
        latency_ms = float(latency_text)
        if not math.isfinite(latency_ms):
            return None
    except (OverflowError, ValueError):
        return None

    return Record(
        ts=ts,
        method=method,
        path=path,
        status=status,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        bytes=byte_count,
    )


def summarize(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Summary:
    """Parse lines and aggregate valid records and malformed-line counts."""
    records: list[Record] = []
    malformed = 0

    for line in lines:
        record = parse_line(line)
        if record is None:
            malformed += 1
        else:
            records.append(record)

    total = len(records)
    by_status = Counter(record.status for record in records)
    by_method = Counter(record.method for record in records)
    path_counts = Counter(record.path for record in records)
    latencies = sorted(record.latency_ms for record in records)

    def nearest_rank(percentile: float) -> float:
        if not latencies:
            return 0.0
        rank = math.ceil(percentile * len(latencies))
        return latencies[rank - 1]

    return Summary(
        total=total,
        malformed=malformed,
        by_status=dict(by_status),
        by_method=dict(by_method),
        p50_latency_ms=nearest_rank(0.50),
        p95_latency_ms=nearest_rank(0.95),
        bytes_total=sum(record.bytes for record in records),
        error_rate=(sum(record.status >= 500 for record in records) / total)
        if total
        else 0.0,
        top_paths=sorted(path_counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:5],
    )

diff --git a/logstats/parse.py b/logstats/parse.py
index fcc184a..30b1cb4 100644
--- a/logstats/parse.py
+++ b/logstats/parse.py
@@ -1 +1,111 @@
-"""Implement parse_line and summarize here. See FORMAT.md."""
+"""Parse access log lines and summarize their records."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections import Counter
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+import math
+from typing import Iterable
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Record:
+    ts: datetime
+    method: str
+    path: str
+    status: int
+    latency_ms: float
+    bytes: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Summary:
+    total: int
+    malformed: int
+    by_status: dict[int, int]
+    by_method: dict[str, int]
+    p50_latency_ms: float
+    p95_latency_ms: float
+    bytes_total: int
+    error_rate: float
+    top_paths: list[tuple[str, int]]
+
+
+def parse_line(line: str) -> Record | None:
+    """Return a parsed record, or ``None`` when the line is malformed."""
+    if not isinstance(line, str):
+        return None
+
+    fields = line.split()
+    if len(fields) not in (5, 6):
+        return None
+
+    timestamp, method, path, status_text, latency_text = fields[:5]
+    bytes_text = fields[5] if len(fields) == 6 else "0"
+
+    try:
+        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+        if ts.tzinfo is None or ts.utcoffset() is None:
+            return None
+        ts = ts.astimezone(timezone.utc)
+
+        if not status_text.lstrip("+-").isdigit():
+            return None
+        if not bytes_text.lstrip("+-").isdigit():
+            return None
+        status = int(status_text)
+        byte_count = int(bytes_text)
+        latency_ms = float(latency_text)
+        if not math.isfinite(latency_ms):
+            return None
+    except (OverflowError, ValueError):
+        return None
+
+    return Record(
+        ts=ts,
+        method=method,
+        path=path,
+        status=status,
+        latency_ms=latency_ms,
+        bytes=byte_count,
+    )
+
+
+def summarize(lines: Iterable[str]) -> Summary:
+    """Parse lines and aggregate valid records and malformed-line counts."""
+    records: list[Record] = []
+    malformed = 0
+
+    for line in lines:
+        record = parse_line(line)
+        if record is None:
+            malformed += 1
+        else:
+            records.append(record)
+
+    total = len(records)
+    by_status = Counter(record.status for record in records)
+    by_method = Counter(record.method for record in records)
+    path_counts = Counter(record.path for record in records)
+    latencies = sorted(record.latency_ms for record in records)
+
+    def nearest_rank(percentile: float) -> float:
+        if not latencies:
+            return 0.0
+        rank = math.ceil(percentile * len(latencies))
+        return latencies[rank - 1]
+
+    return Summary(
+        total=total,
+        malformed=malformed,
+        by_status=dict(by_status),
+        by_method=dict(by_method),
+        p50_latency_ms=nearest_rank(0.50),
+        p95_latency_ms=nearest_rank(0.95),
+        bytes_total=sum(record.bytes for record in records),
+        error_rate=(sum(record.status >= 500 for record in records) / total)
+        if total
+        else 0.0,
+        top_paths=sorted(path_counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:5],
+    )

Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. from inv.warehouse import Warehouse


def test_independent_warehouses():
    a = Warehouse("a")
    a.restock("bolt", 5)
    b = Warehouse("b")
    assert b.report() == {}
    b.restock("nut", 2)
    assert a.report() == {"bolt": 5}
    assert len(b.history) == 1


def test_default_restock_tags_are_independent():
    a = Warehouse("a")
    b = Warehouse("b")
    a.restock("bolt", 1)
    b.restock("nut", 1)

    a.stock["bolt"].tags.append("fragile")

    assert b.stock["nut"].tags == []

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Item:
    sku: str
    qty: int = 0
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)


class Warehouse:
    def __init__(self, name, stock=None, history=None):
        self.name = name
        self.stock = {} if stock is None else stock
        self.history = [] if history is None else history

    def restock(self, sku, qty, tags=None):
        item = self.stock.get(sku)
        if item is None:
            item = Item(sku, 0, [] if tags is None else tags)
            self.stock[sku] = item
        item.qty += qty
        self.history.append(("restock", sku, qty))

    def ship(self, sku, qty):
        item = self.stock[sku]
        if item.qty < qty:
            raise ValueError("insufficient stock")
        item.qty -= qty
        self.history.append(("ship", sku, qty))

    def report(self):
        return {sku: item.qty for sku, item in sorted(self.stock.items())}

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def next_run(now: datetime, hour: int, minute: int, tz: str) -> datetime:
    """Next hour:minute in tz strictly after now. `now` may be naive (treated as UTC) or aware."""
    if now.tzinfo is None:
        now = now.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    zone = ZoneInfo(tz)
    now_utc = now.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    today = now.astimezone(zone).date()
    candidate = datetime(today.year, today.month, today.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=zone)
    if candidate.astimezone(timezone.utc) <= now_utc:
        tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
        candidate = datetime(tomorrow.year, tomorrow.month, tomorrow.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=zone)
    return candidate

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

from datetime import datetime, timezone

from sched import next_run


def test_result_is_after_now_late_evening_utc():
    now = datetime(2026, 6, 1, 23, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc)   # already 01:30 on June 2 in Berlin
    nxt = next_run(now, 1, 0, "Europe/Berlin")
    assert nxt > now
    assert (nxt.year, nxt.month, nxt.day, nxt.hour) == (2026, 6, 3, 1)


def test_wall_clock_hour_is_preserved_across_dst_start():
    now = datetime(2026, 3, 28, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    nxt = next_run(now, 9, 0, "Europe/Berlin")
    assert (nxt.year, nxt.month, nxt.day, nxt.hour, nxt.minute) == (2026, 3, 29, 9, 0)
    assert nxt.utcoffset().total_seconds() == 2 * 60 * 60

import threading
import time


class Counter:
    """Named counters. Intended to be shared across request-handler threads."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._values = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def incr(self, name, by=1):
        with self._lock:
            current = self._values.get(name, 0)
            time.sleep(0)  # yield, simulates real work between read and write
            self._values[name] = current + by

    def get(self, name):
        with self._lock:
            return self._values.get(name, 0)

    def snapshot(self):
        with self._lock:
            return dict(self._values)

    def reset(self, name=None):
        with self._lock:
            if name is None:
                self._values.clear()
            else:
                self._values.pop(name, None)

Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

import threading

from metrics import Counter


def test_no_lost_updates():
    c = Counter()

    def work():
        for _ in range(2000):
            c.incr("hits")

    ts = [threading.Thread(target=work) for _ in range(8)]
    [t.start() for t in ts]; [t.join() for t in ts]
    assert c.get("hits") == 16000


def test_snapshot_is_plain_dict_copy():
    c = Counter()
    c.incr("hits", 3)

    snapshot = c.snapshot()

    assert type(snapshot) is dict
    snapshot["hits"] = 0
    assert c.get("hits") == 3

from .registry import get


def export_records(records, fmt):
    """records: list of dicts with identical keys. Returns bytes."""
    exporter_cls = get(fmt)
    return exporter_cls().dump(records)


def export_to_file(records, fmt, path):
    exporter_cls = get(fmt)
    path = str(path)
    if not path.endswith(exporter_cls.extension):
        path += exporter_cls.extension
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(exporter_cls().dump(records))
    return path

import csv as csv_module
import io

from ..registry import Exporter, register


@register
class CSVExporter(Exporter):
    name = "csv"
    extension = ".csv"

    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        buf = io.StringIO()
        if records:
            writer = csv_module.DictWriter(
                buf,
                fieldnames=list(records[0].keys()),
                lineterminator="\n",
            )
            writer.writeheader()
            writer.writerows(records)
        return buf.getvalue().encode()

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import ClassVar, TypeVar


class UnknownFormat(ValueError):
    """Raised when no exporter is registered for a format name."""

    def __init__(self, name, known_names):
        self.name = name
        self.known_names = tuple(known_names)
        known = ", ".join(self.known_names) or "none"
        super().__init__(f"Unknown format {name!r}. Known formats: {known}")


class Exporter(ABC):
    name: ClassVar[str]
    extension: ClassVar[str]

    @abstractmethod
    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        """Serialize records to bytes."""
        raise NotImplementedError


ExporterClass = TypeVar("ExporterClass", bound=type[Exporter])
_exporters: dict[str, type[Exporter]] = {}


def register(exporter_cls: ExporterClass) -> ExporterClass:
    """Register an exporter class and return it for decorator use."""
    name = exporter_cls.name
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
        raise ValueError("Exporter name must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(exporter_cls.extension, str) or not exporter_cls.extension:
        raise ValueError("Exporter extension must be a non-empty string")
    if name in _exporters:
        raise ValueError(f"Exporter already registered for format {name!r}")
    _exporters[name] = exporter_cls
    return exporter_cls


def get(name: str) -> type[Exporter]:
    try:
        return _exporters[name]
    except KeyError:
        raise UnknownFormat(name, names()) from None


def names() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    return tuple(_exporters)

+import csv as csv_module
+import io
+
+from ..registry import Exporter, register
+
+
+@register
+class CSVExporter(Exporter):
+    name = "csv"
+    extension = ".csv"
+
+    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
+        buf = io.StringIO()
+        if records:
+            writer = csv_module.DictWriter(
+                buf,
+                fieldnames=list(records[0].keys()),
+                lineterminator="\n",
+            )
+            writer.writeheader()
+            writer.writerows(records)
+        return buf.getvalue().encode()

+import json
+
+from ..registry import Exporter, register
+
+
+@register
+class JSONExporter(Exporter):

+from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
+
+from ..registry import Exporter, register
+
+
+@register
+class XMLExporter(Exporter):
+    name = "xml"
+    extension = ".xml"
+
+    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
+        parts = ["<records>"]
+        for record in records:
+            parts.append("  <record>")
+            for key, value in record.items():
+                parts.append(f"    <{key}>{escape(str(value))}</{key}>")
+            parts.append("  </record>")
+        parts.append("</records>")
+        return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()

+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from typing import ClassVar, TypeVar
+
+
+class UnknownFormat(ValueError):
+    """Raised when no exporter is registered for a format name."""
+
+    def __init__(self, name, known_names):
+        self.name = name
+        self.known_names = tuple(known_names)
+        known = ", ".join(self.known_names) or "none"
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown format {name!r}. Known formats: {known}")
+

import json

import export.registry as registry
from export import (
    Exporter,
    UnknownFormat,
    export_records,
    export_to_file,
    get,
    names,
    register,
)

R = [{"id": 1, "name": "a&b"}, {"id": 2, "name": "c"}]


def test_csv():
    assert export_records(R, "csv") == b"id,name\n1,a&b\n2,c\n"


def test_json():
    assert json.loads(export_records(R, "json")) == R


def test_xml():
    assert b"<name>a&amp;b</name>" in export_records(R, "xml")


def test_file_extension(tmp_path):
    p = export_to_file(R, "json", tmp_path / "out")
    assert p.endswith(".json")


def test_unknown():
    try:
        export_records(R, "yaml")
    except UnknownFormat as error:
        assert "csv, json, xml" in str(error)
    else:
        raise AssertionError


def test_registered_exporter(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "_exporters", {})

    @register
    class TextExporter(Exporter):
        name = "test-format"
        extension = ".txt"

        def dump(self, records):
            return b"custom"

    assert get("test-format") is TextExporter
    assert "test-format" in names()
    assert export_records(R, "test-format") == b"custom"

from xml.sax.saxutils import escape

from ..registry import Exporter, register


@register
class XMLExporter(Exporter):
    name = "xml"
    extension = ".xml"

    def dump(self, records) -> bytes:
        parts = ["<records>"]
        for record in records:
            parts.append("  <record>")
            for key, value in record.items():
                parts.append(f"    <{key}>{escape(str(value))}</{key}>")
            parts.append("  </record>")
        parts.append("</records>")
        return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()

prompt: "Migrate the `fetcher` package from blocking I/O to asyncio while keeping behaviour:\n\n- `fetcher.Client` becomes an async client: `async get(url)`, `async get_many(urls)`,\n  `async with` support, and `close()` becomes `async close()`.\n- Transport is injected: `Client(transport)` where `transport` is an async callable\n  `async (url) -> bytes`. The default transport uses `asyncio.sleep` to simulate latency\n  as the sync one uses `time.sleep`.\n- `get_many` runs requests concurrently with a concurrency limit `max_concurrency`\n  (constructor arg, default 5). Results keep input order. Errors for individual URLs\n  are returned as `FetchError` instances in the result list, not raised.\n- Retries: same policy as today (up to `retries` attempts, exponential backoff using\n  `asyncio.sleep`), retry only on `TransientError`.\n- `aggregate.summarize(client, urls)` becomes `async` and keeps its return shape.\n- Keep a thin sync wrapper `fetcher.sync.fetch_all(urls, transport=None)` that\
  \ runs the\n  async code with `asyncio.run` for callers that are not async.\n\nPort the existing tests to pytest-asyncio or plain `asyncio.run`, keep them passing, and\nrun them.\n"

from .client import FetchError


async def summarize(client, urls):
    results = await client.get_many(urls)
    ok = [r for r in results if not isinstance(r, FetchError)]
    failed = [r.url for r in results if isinstance(r, FetchError)]
    return {"ok": len(ok), "failed": failed, "bytes": sum(len(r) for r in ok)}

import asyncio


class FetchError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, url, cause):
        super().__init__(f"{url}: {cause}")
        self.url = url
        self.cause = cause


class TransientError(Exception):
    pass


async def default_transport(url):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    if url.endswith("/404"):
        raise KeyError("not found")
    return f"payload for {url}".encode()


class Client:
    def __init__(self, transport=None, retries=3, backoff=0.01, max_concurrency=5):
        if max_concurrency < 1:
            raise ValueError("max_concurrency must be at least 1")
        self.transport = default_transport if transport is None else transport
        self.retries = retries
        self.backoff = backoff
        self.max_concurrency = max_concurrency
        self._semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrency)
        self.closed = False
        self.calls = 0

    async def get(self, url):
        if self.closed:
            raise RuntimeError("client closed")
        delay = self.backoff
        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 1):
            self.calls += 1
            try:
                return await self.transport(url)
            except TransientError:
                if attempt == self.retries:
                    raise
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                delay *= 2

    async def get_many(self, urls):
        async def fetch(url):
            try:
                async with self._semaphore:
                    return await self.get(url)
            except Exception as e:
                return FetchError(url, e)

        return await asyncio.gather(*(fetch(url) for url in urls))

    async def close(self):
        self.closed = True

    async def __aenter__(self):
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        await self.close()

Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. import asyncio

from .client import Client


def fetch_all(urls, transport=None):
    async def fetch():
        async with Client(transport=transport) as client:
            return await client.get_many(urls)

    return asyncio.run(fetch())

import asyncio

from fetcher import Client, FetchError, TransientError, aggregate
from fetcher.sync import fetch_all


def test_get_and_many():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as client:
            assert await client.get("http://x/1") == b"payload for http://x/1"
            results = await client.get_many(["http://x/1", "http://x/404"])
            assert results[0].startswith(b"payload")
            assert isinstance(results[1], FetchError)
        assert client.closed

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_retry_then_succeed():
    async def run():
        attempts = {"n": 0}

        async def flaky(url):
            attempts["n"] += 1
            if attempts["n"] < 3:
                raise TransientError("try again")
            return b"ok"

        client = Client(transport=flaky, retries=3)
        assert await client.get("u") == b"ok"
        assert client.calls == 3

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_get_many_limits_concurrency_and_keeps_order():
    async def run():
        active = 0
        max_active = 0

        async def transport(url):
            nonlocal active, max_active
            active += 1
            max_active = max(max_active, active)
            await asyncio.sleep((5 - int(url)) * 0.001)
            active -= 1
            return url.encode()

        client = Client(transport=transport, max_concurrency=2)
        results = await client.get_many(["1", "2", "3", "4"])
        assert results == [b"1", b"2", b"3", b"4"]
        assert max_active == 2

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_summarize():
    async def run():
        async with Client() as client:
            assert await aggregate.summarize(
                client, ["http://x/1", "http://x/404"]
            ) == {
                "ok": 1,
                "failed": ["http://x/404"],
                "bytes": len(b"payload for http://x/1"),
            }

    asyncio.run(run())


def test_sync_fetch_all():
    async def transport(url):
        return url.encode()

    assert fetch_all(["u1", "u2"], transport=transport) == [b"u1", b"u2"]

from decimal import Decimal

from billing import build_invoice, percent_off, invoice_total, line_totals, TaxRule


def test_simple_total():
    inv = build_invoice("A1", [("x", "10.00", 2), ("y", "0.50", 1)])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("20.50")
    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("20.50")


def test_with_tax():
    inv = build_invoice("A2", [("x", "100.00", 1)], TaxRule("DE", Decimal("0.19")))
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("119.00")


def test_discount_whole_numbers():
    inv = build_invoice("A3", [("x", "100.00", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10"))])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("90.00")


def test_invoice_total_matches_rounded_discounted_lines():
    discount = percent_off("TEN", "10")
    inv = build_invoice("A4", [("x", "0.05", 1, discount)] * 3)

    assert line_totals(inv) == [Decimal("0.05")] * 3
    assert invoice_total(inv) == sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("0.15")

"""Totals. The PDF renderer shows line_totals(); the amount charged is invoice_total()."""
from decimal import Decimal

from .discounts import apply_discount
from .invoice import Invoice
from .money import round_money
from .tax import tax_for


def line_totals(inv: Invoice) -> list[Decimal]:
    """Per-line amounts as printed on the invoice, discount applied per line."""
    return [apply_discount(li.unit_price * li.qty, li.discount) for li in inv.lines]


def invoice_total(inv: Invoice) -> Decimal:
    """Amount charged: sum of lines after discount, plus tax on that sum."""
    net = sum(line_totals(inv), Decimal("0.00"))
    return round_money(net + tax_for(net, inv.tax_rule))

import re
import unicodedata

_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def email_key(email):
    return email.strip().casefold()


def name_key(name):
    """Key for matching names: case-folded, accent-free, single spaces."""
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", name).casefold()
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", s)
    s = "".join(char for char in s if not unicodedata.category(char).startswith("M"))
    return _WS.sub(" ", s.strip())


def dedupe(records):
    """records: list of dicts with 'name' and 'email'. Returns survivors in first-seen order."""
    seen_names, seen_emails, out = set(), set(), []
    for r in records:
        nk, ek = name_key(r["name"]), email_key(r["email"])
        duplicate = nk in seen_names or ek in seen_emails
        seen_names.add(nk)
        seen_emails.add(ek)
        if not duplicate:
            out.append(r)
    return out
