{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Resolve package requirements against a version index."""

from functools import total_ordering
import re


class ResolutionError(Exception):
    """Raised when package requirements have no consistent solution."""


@total_ordering
class Version:
    """A dotted numeric version that retains its input spelling."""

    __slots__ = ("_parts", "_normalized", "_text")

    def __init__(self, s):
        text = str(s)
        pieces = text.split(".")
        if not pieces or any(not piece.isdigit() for piece in pieces):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid version: {text!r}")
        parts = tuple(int(piece) for piece in pieces)
        normalized = list(parts)
        while len(normalized) > 1 and normalized[-1] == 0:
            normalized.pop()
        self._parts = parts
        self._normalized = tuple(normalized)
        self._text = text

    def __str__(self):
        return self._text

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Version({self._text!r})"

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self._normalized)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self._normalized == other._normalized

    def __lt__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        width = max(len(self._parts), len(other._parts))
        left = self._parts + (0,) * (width - len(self._parts))
        right = other._parts + (0,) * (width - len(other._parts))
        return left < right


_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+)(.*)$")
_CLAUSE_RE = re.compile(r"\s*(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s*")


class Constraint:
    """A package name with zero or more version clauses."""

    __slots__ = ("name", "_clauses")

    def __init__(self, name, clauses=()):
        self.name = name
        self._clauses = tuple(clauses)

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, requirement):
        if not isinstance(requirement, str):
            raise ValueError("requirement must be a string")

        match = _NAME_RE.fullmatch(requirement.strip())
        if match is None:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")

        name, remainder = match.groups()
        clauses = []
        if remainder:
            for clause_text in remainder.split(","):
                clause_match = _CLAUSE_RE.fullmatch(clause_text)
                if clause_match is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")
                operator, version_text = clause_match.groups()
                clauses.append((operator, Version(version_text)))
        return cls(name, clauses)

    def allows(self, version):
        if not isinstance(version, Version):
            version = Version(version)

        for operator, expected in self._clauses:
            if operator == "==" and version != expected:
                return False
            if operator == "!=" and version == expected:
                return False
            if operator == "<" and not version < expected:
                return False
            if operator == "<=" and version > expected:
                return False
            if operator == ">" and not version > expected:
                return False
            if operator == ">=" and version < expected:
                return False
        return True


class _DeadEnd(Exception):
    def __init__(self, package, depth):
        super().__init__(package)
        self.package = package
        self.depth = depth


def resolve(roots, index):
    """Return the preferred satisfying version for each reachable package."""
    catalogue = {}
    for package, package_versions in index.items():
        entries = []
        for version_text, requirements in package_versions.items():
            version = Version(version_text)
            dependencies = tuple(Constraint.parse(requirement) for requirement in requirements)
            entries.append((version, dependencies))
        catalogue[package] = sorted(entries, key=lambda entry: entry[0], reverse=True)

    constraints = {}
    for root in roots:
        requirement = Constraint.parse(root)
        constraints.setdefault(requirement.name, []).append(requirement)

    def satisfies_all(version, requirements):
        return all(requirement.allows(version) for requirement in requirements)

    def candidate_dependencies(entry, active_constraints, assignments):
        """Check whether a version's direct dependencies still have a domain."""
        grouped = {}
        for dependency in entry[1]:
            grouped.setdefault(dependency.name, []).append(dependency)

        for package, requirements in grouped.items():
            if package in assignments:
                if not satisfies_all(assignments[package], requirements):
                    return package
                continue

            combined = active_constraints.get(package, []) + requirements
            candidates = catalogue.get(package, ())
            if not any(satisfies_all(version, combined) for version, _ in candidates):
                return package
        return None

    def propagate(active_constraints, assignments):
        """Apply assigned dependencies and forced domains until stable."""
        active_constraints = {name: list(reqs) for name, reqs in active_constraints.items()}
        assignments = dict(assignments)

        while True:
            for package, version in assignments.items():
                if not satisfies_all(version, active_constraints.get(package, ())):
                    raise _DeadEnd(package, len(assignments))

            domains = {}
            for package in sorted(active_constraints):
                if package in assignments:
                    continue

                raw_domain = [
                    entry
                    for entry in catalogue.get(package, ())
                    if satisfies_all(entry[0], active_constraints[package])
                ]
                if not raw_domain:
                    raise _DeadEnd(package, len(assignments) + 1)

                domain = []
                rejected_by = []
                for entry in raw_domain:
                    blocker = candidate_dependencies(entry, active_constraints, assignments)
                    if blocker is None:
                        domain.append(entry)
                    else:
                        rejected_by.append(blocker)
                if not domain:
                    blocker = rejected_by[0]
                    raise _DeadEnd(blocker, len(assignments) + 1)
                domains[package] = domain

            forced = next(
                ((package, domain[0]) for package, domain in domains.items() if len(domain) == 1),
                None,
            )
            if forced is None:
                return active_constraints, assignments, domains

            package, entry = forced
            assignments[package] = entry[0]
            for dependency in entry[1]:
                active_constraints.setdefault(dependency.name, []).append(dependency)

    def search(active_constraints, assignments):

Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? import unittest

from resolver import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve


class VersionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_versions_compare_numerically_and_normalize_missing_components(self):
        self.assertEqual(Version("1.0"), Version("1"))
        self.assertEqual(hash(Version("1.0")), hash(Version("1")))
        self.assertGreater(Version("1.10"), Version("1.9"))
        self.assertEqual(str(Version("01.0")), "01.0")

    def test_constraint_parses_and_combines_clauses(self):
        constraint = Constraint.parse("json>=2,<3,!=2.5")

        self.assertEqual(constraint.name, "json")
        self.assertTrue(constraint.allows(Version("2.9")))
        self.assertFalse(constraint.allows(Version("2.5")))
        self.assertFalse(constraint.allows(Version("3")))

    def test_all_constraint_operators(self):
        cases = (
            ("pkg==2", "2.0", "3"),
            ("pkg!=2", "3", "2.0"),
            ("pkg<2", "1.9", "2"),
            ("pkg<=2", "2.0", "3"),
            ("pkg>2", "2.1", "2"),
            ("pkg>=2", "2.0", "1.9"),
        )
        for requirement, accepted, rejected in cases:
            with self.subTest(requirement=requirement):
                constraint = Constraint.parse(requirement)
                self.assertTrue(constraint.allows(Version(accepted)))
                self.assertFalse(constraint.allows(Version(rejected)))


class ResolveTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_prefers_highest_satisfying_version_and_ignores_unreachable(self):
        index = {
            "app": {"1": ["web>=2"]},
            "web": {"1": [], "2": [], "3": []},
            "unused": {"99": []},
        }

        self.assertEqual(resolve(["app"], index), {"app": "1", "web": "3"})

    def test_backtracks_to_satisfy_conflicting_transitive_requirements(self):
        index = {
            "app": {"1": ["web", "db"]},
            "web": {"1": [], "2": ["json>=3"]},
            "db": {"1": ["json<3"]},
            "json": {"2": [], "3": []},
        }

        self.assertEqual(
            resolve(["app"], index),
            {"app": "1", "web": "1", "db": "1", "json": "2"},
        )

    def test_alphabetical_preference_is_used_with_backtracking(self):
        index = {
            "x": {"1": ["shared<2"], "2": ["shared>=2"]},
            "y": {"1": ["shared>=2"], "2": ["shared<2"]},
            "shared": {"1": [], "2": []},
        }

        self.assertEqual(
            resolve(["y", "x"], index),
            {"x": "2", "y": "1", "shared": "2"},
        )

    def test_cycles_are_allowed(self):
        index = {
            "a": {"1": ["b>=1"]},
            "b": {"1": ["a>=1"]},
        }

        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], index), {"a": "1", "b": "1"})

    def test_error_names_unsatisfied_leaf_package(self):
        index = {
            "a": {"1": ["b<1"]},
            "b": {"1": [], "2": []},
        }

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, r"package b"):
            resolve(["a"], index)

    def test_backtracks_when_dependency_cycle_conflicts(self):
        index = {
            "a": {"1": ["b<2"], "2": ["b>=2"]},
            "b": {"1": [], "2": ["a<2"]},
        }

        self.assertEqual(resolve(["a"], index), {"a": "1", "b": "1"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).

Refactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.
"""


def dedupe_rows(rows):
    seen_ids = set()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if r.event_id in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(r.event_id)
        out.append(r)
    return out

+def test_report_deduplication_uses_bounded_event_id_comparisons():
+    class CountedEventId(str):
+        comparisons = 0
+
+        def __eq__(self, other):
+            type(self).comparisons += 1
+            return super().__eq__(other)
+
+        def __hash__(self):
+            return str.__hash__(self)
+

+    ]

+

+        {"tenant": "*", "service": "*", "cpu_seconds": 2500.0, "bytes_out": 25000, "events": 2500},
+    ]

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_4","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md && sed -n '1,240p' reporting/report.py && sed -n '1,260p' reporting/aggregate.py && sed -n '1,260p' reporting/dedupe.py && sed -n '1,260p' tests/test_report.py && cat README.md && cat input.yaml\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\nfrom .dedupe import dedupe_rows\nfrom .aggregate import aggregate\n\n\ndef build_report(rows):\n    \"\"\"Returns list of dicts, one per (tenant, service), plus a totals row at the end.\"\"\"\n    rows = dedupe_rows(rows)\n    agg = aggregate(rows)\n    out = []\n    tot_cpu, tot_bytes, tot_n = 0.0, 0, 0\n    for (tenant, service), (cpu, byts, n) in agg.items():\n        out.append({\"tenant\": tenant, \"service\": service, \"cpu_seconds\": round(cpu, 3), \"bytes_out\": byts, \"events\": n})\n        tot_cpu += cpu; tot_bytes += byts; tot_n += n\n    out.append({\"tenant\": \"*\", \"service\": \"*\", \"cpu_seconds\": round(tot_cpu, 3), \"bytes_out\": tot_bytes, \"events\": tot_n})\n    return out\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\n\ndef aggregate(rows):\n    \"\"\"Per (tenant, service): total cpu_seconds, total bytes_out, event count. Sorted by tenant then service.\"\"\"\n    acc = defaultdict(lambda: [0.0, 0, 0])\n    for r in rows:\n        a = acc[(r.tenant, r.service)]\n        a[0] += r.cpu_seconds\n        a[1] += r.bytes_out\n        a[2] += 1\n    return {k: tuple(v) for k, v in sorted(acc.items())}\n\"\"\"Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).\n\nRefactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef dedupe_rows(rows):\n    seen_ids = []\n    out = []\n    for r in rows:\n        if r.event_id in seen_ids:\n            continue\n        seen_ids.append(r.event_id)\n        out.append(r)\n    return out\nfrom reporting import parse_rows, build_report\n\n\ndef test_small_report():\n    rows = parse_rows([\"e1,acme,api,1.5,100\", \"e2,acme,api,0.5,50\", \"e2,acme,api,0.5,50\", \"e3,beta,web,2,10\"])\n    rep = build_report(rows)\n    assert rep[0] == {\"tenant\": \"acme\", \"service\": \"api\", \"cpu_seconds\": 2.0, \"bytes_out\": 150, \"events\": 2}\n    assert rep[-1][\"events\"] == 3\n# reporting\n\nNightly usage report. `python -m pytest` runs the tests.\ntask: t15_perf_regression\nprompt: 'Ops ticket: \"The nightly usage report used to finish in under a minute. Since last\n\n  week''s refactor it runs for over an hour on the same data (about 30k rows) and the ops\n\n  team kills it. Output looks correct when it does finish.\"\n\n\n  The `reporting` package is in this repo. Find the root cause, fix it without changing\n\n  the output or the public API, and add a regression test under `tests/` that would catch\n\n  it. Run the full test suite.\n\n  '\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

from reporting import UsageRow, build_report, parse_rows


def test_small_report():
    rows = parse_rows(["e1,acme,api,1.5,100", "e2,acme,api,0.5,50", "e2,acme,api,0.5,50", "e3,beta,web,2,10"])
    rep = build_report(rows)
    assert rep[0] == {"tenant": "acme", "service": "api", "cpu_seconds": 2.0, "bytes_out": 150, "events": 2}
    assert rep[-1]["events"] == 3


def test_report_deduplication_uses_bounded_event_id_comparisons():
    class CountedEventId(str):
        comparisons = 0

        def __eq__(self, other):
            type(self).comparisons += 1
            return super().__eq__(other)

        def __hash__(self):
            return str.__hash__(self)

    rows = [
        UsageRow(CountedEventId(f"event-{i:05d}"), "acme", "api", 1.0, 10)
        for i in range(2500)
    ]

    report = build_report(rows)

    assert report == [
        {"tenant": "acme", "service": "api", "cpu_seconds": 2500.0, "bytes_out": 25000, "events": 2500},
        {"tenant": "*", "service": "*", "cpu_seconds": 2500.0, "bytes_out": 25000, "events": 2500},
    ]
    assert CountedEventId.comparisons <= len(rows) * 2

from copy import deepcopy


class PatchError(Exception):
    pass


class PointerError(PatchError):
    pass


def _pointer_tokens(pointer):
    if not isinstance(pointer, str):
        raise PointerError("JSON Pointer must be a string")
    if pointer == "":
        return ()
    if not pointer.startswith("/"):
        raise PointerError("JSON Pointer must be empty or start with '/'")

    tokens = []
    for token in pointer[1:].split("/"):
        decoded = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(token):
            char = token[i]
            if char != "~":
                decoded.append(char)
                i += 1
                continue
            if i + 1 == len(token) or token[i + 1] not in "01":
                raise PointerError("invalid '~' escape in JSON Pointer")
            decoded.append("~" if token[i + 1] == "0" else "/")
            i += 2
        tokens.append("".join(decoded))
    return tuple(tokens)


def _array_index(token, length, *, allow_end=False, allow_dash=False):
    if allow_dash and token == "-":
        return length
    if not token or (token != "0" and token[0] not in "123456789"):
        raise PointerError("invalid array index")
    if any(char < "0" or char > "9" for char in token):
        raise PointerError("invalid array index")
    limit = str(length)
    if len(token) > len(limit) or (len(token) == len(limit) and token > limit):
        raise PointerError("array index out of range")
    index = int(token)
    if index == length and not allow_end:
        raise PointerError("array index out of range")
    return index


def _child(value, token):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        if token not in value:
            raise PointerError("object member does not exist")
        return value[token]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return value[_array_index(token, len(value))]
    raise PointerError("pointer traverses a non-container value")


def _read_tokens(doc, tokens):
    value = doc
    for token in tokens:
        value = _child(value, token)
    return value


def resolve_pointer(doc, pointer):
    """Resolve a JSON Pointer against a document."""
    return _read_tokens(doc, _pointer_tokens(pointer))


def _parent_at(doc, tokens):
    if not tokens:
        return None, None
    parent = _read_tokens(doc, tokens[:-1])
    return parent, tokens[-1]


def _add(doc, tokens, value):
    value = deepcopy(value)
    if not tokens:
        return value
    parent, token = _parent_at(doc, tokens)
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        parent[token] = value
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        parent.insert(
            _array_index(token, len(parent), allow_end=True, allow_dash=True), value
        )
    else:
        raise PointerError("add parent is not an object or array")
    return doc


def _remove(doc, tokens):
    if not tokens:
        return None, doc
    parent, token = _parent_at(doc, tokens)
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if token not in parent:
            raise PointerError("object member does not exist")
        return doc, parent.pop(token)
    if isinstance(parent, list):
        index = _array_index(token, len(parent))
        return doc, parent.pop(index)
    raise PointerError("remove parent is not an object or array")


def _replace(doc, tokens, value):
    value = deepcopy(value)
    if not tokens:
        return value
    parent, token = _parent_at(doc, tokens)
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if token not in parent:
            raise PointerError("object member does not exist")
        parent[token] = value
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        parent[_array_index(token, len(parent))] = value
    else:
        raise PointerError("replace parent is not an object or array")
    return doc


def _equal(left, right):
    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
        return isinstance(left, bool) and isinstance(right, bool) and left == right
    if isinstance(left, (int, float)) and isinstance(right, (int, float)):
        return left == right
    if isinstance(left, dict) and isinstance(right, dict):
        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(
            _equal(left[key], right[key]) for key in left
        )
    if isinstance(left, list) and isinstance(right, list):
        return len(left) == len(right) and all(
            _equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right)
        )
    return type(left) is type(right) and left == right


def _apply_one(doc, operation):
    if not isinstance(operation, dict):
        raise PatchError("each operation must be an object")
    op = operation.get("op")
    if not isinstance(op, str):
        raise PatchError("operation 'op' must be a string")
    if op not in {"add", "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", "test"}:
        raise PatchError("unknown operation")
    if "path" not in operation or not isinstance(operation["path"], str):
        raise PatchError("operation 'path' must be a string")
    path = _pointer_tokens(operation["path"])

    if op in {"add", "replace", "test"} and "value" not in operation:
        raise PatchError("operation requires 'value'")
    if op in {"move", "copy"}:
        if "from" not in operation or not isinstance(operation["from"], str):
            raise PatchError("operation 'from' must be a string")
        source = _pointer_tokens(operation["from"])

    if op == "add":
        return _add(doc, path, operation["value"])
    if op == "remove":
        return _remove(doc, path)[0]
    if op == "replace":
        return _replace(doc, path, operation["value"])
    if op == "move":
        if len(source) < len(path) and path[: len(source)] == source:
            raise PatchError("cannot move a value into one of its children")
        value = _read_tokens(doc, source)
        if source == path:
            return doc
        doc, value = _remove(doc, source)
        return _add(doc, path, value)
    if op == "copy":
        return _add(doc, path, _read_tokens(doc, source))

    if not _equal(_read_tokens(doc, path), operation["value"]):
        raise PatchError("test operation failed")
    return doc


def _commit(doc, result):
    if isinstance(doc, dict) and isinstance(result, dict):
        doc.clear()
        doc.update(result)
        return doc
    if isinstance(doc, list) and isinstance(result, list):
        doc[:] = result
        return doc
    # Python cannot rebind the caller's reference when a patch replaces the root
    # with a different type or the original root is immutable.
    return result


def apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False):
    """Apply a JSON Patch sequence atomically and return the resulting document."""

+def _array_index(token, length, *, allow_end=False, allow_dash=False):

+
+def _remove(doc, tokens):

+    parent, token = _parent_at(doc, tokens)
+    if isinstance(parent, dict):

+def _replace(doc, tokens, value):

+    return doc

+
+def _equal(left, right):

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_3","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat jsonpatch/SPEC.md && cat jsonpatch/core.py'","aggregated_output":"# Spec\n\n## JSON Pointer (RFC 6901)\n\n`resolve_pointer(doc, pointer) -> value`\n\n- `\"\"` is the whole document. Otherwise the pointer starts with `/` and each token is\n  unescaped: `~1` -> `/`, `~0` -> `~` (in that order).\n- Object tokens are keys. Array tokens must be a non-negative integer with no leading\n  zeros (`\"0\"` ok, `\"01\"` not ok); `\"-\"` is only valid for `add` as \"append\".\n- Anything invalid raises `PointerError` (subclass of `PatchError`).\n\n## JSON Patch (RFC 6902)\n\n`apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False) -> new_doc`\n\n`patch` is a list of operation dicts with `op` in `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`,\n`copy`, `test`, plus `path` and, where applicable, `value` or `from`.\n\n- `add`: object key set or array insert at index (index == len allowed, `-` appends);\n  replacing the root is allowed.\n- `remove`: target must exist.\n- `replace`: target must exist.\n- `move`: `from` must exist; `from` must not be a proper prefix of `path` (cannot move a\n  value into one of its own children); equivalent to remove then add.\n- `copy`: `from` must exist; deep copy; then add.\n- `test`: deep equality of `value` with the target. Numbers compare by value\n  (`1 == 1.0`), but `True != 1`.\n- Operations apply in order. If any operation fails, raise `PatchError` and leave the\n  input document unchanged (atomic). With `in_place=True` the input document is mutated\n  on success and untouched on failure; otherwise the input is never mutated.\n- Unknown `op`, missing required fields, or wrong types raise `PatchError`.\nclass PatchError(Exception):\n    pass\n\n\nclass PointerError(PatchError):\n    pass\n\n\ndef resolve_pointer(doc, pointer):\n    raise NotImplementedError\n\n\ndef apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False):\n    raise NotImplementedError\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_9","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc 'cat /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md'","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

import unittest

from jsonpatch import PatchError, PointerError, apply_patch, resolve_pointer


class ResolvePointerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_resolves_root_objects_arrays_and_escaped_tokens(self):
        document = {"a/b": {"m~n": ["first", "second"]}, "": "empty", "~1": "ordered"}
        self.assertIs(resolve_pointer(document, ""), document)
        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(document, "/a~1b/m~0n/1"), "second")
        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(document, "/"), "empty")
        self.assertEqual(resolve_pointer(document, "/~01"), "ordered")

    def test_rejects_invalid_pointer_syntax_and_traversal(self):
        document = {"items": ["x"]}
        pointers = (
            "items",
            "/items/~",
            "/items/~2",
            "/items/01",
            "/items/-",
            "/items/1",
            "/items/" + "9" * 5000,
            "/missing",
        )
        for pointer in pointers:
            with self.subTest(pointer=pointer):
                with self.assertRaises(PointerError):
                    resolve_pointer(document, pointer)

    def test_pointer_must_be_a_string(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PointerError):
            resolve_pointer({}, None)


class ApplyPatchTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_add_remove_replace_and_root_replacement(self):
        document = {"items": ["a", "c"]}
        result = apply_patch(
            document,
            [
                {"op": "add", "path": "/items/1", "value": "b"},
                {"op": "add", "path": "/items/-", "value": "d"},
                {"op": "replace", "path": "/items/0", "value": "A"},
                {"op": "remove", "path": "/items/2"},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(result, {"items": ["A", "b", "d"]})
        self.assertEqual(document, {"items": ["a", "c"]})
        self.assertEqual(apply_patch(document, [{"op": "add", "path": "", "value": [1]}]), [1])

    def test_move_removes_then_adds_and_rejects_descendants(self):
        result = apply_patch(
            {"items": ["a", "b", "c"]},
            [{"op": "move", "from": "/items/0", "path": "/items/2"}],
        )
        self.assertEqual(result, {"items": ["b", "c", "a"]})
        with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
            apply_patch({"a": {"b": 1}}, [{"op": "move", "from": "/a", "path": "/a/b/c"}])
        with self.assertRaises(PointerError):
            apply_patch({}, [{"op": "move", "from": "/missing", "path": "/missing"}])

    def test_copy_deep_copies_source(self):
        result = apply_patch(
            {"source": {"nested": [1]}},
            [{"op": "copy", "from": "/source", "path": "/copy"}],
        )
        result["copy"]["nested"].append(2)
        self.assertEqual(result["source"], {"nested": [1]})

    def test_test_uses_json_deep_equality(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            apply_patch({"value": [1, {"n": 2}]}, [{"op": "test", "path": "/value", "value": [1.0, {"n": 2.0}]}]),
            {"value": [1, {"n": 2}]},
        )
        for actual, expected in ((True, 1), ([True], [1]), ({"x": True}, {"x": 1})):
            with self.subTest(actual=actual, expected=expected):
                with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
                    apply_patch(actual, [{"op": "test", "path": "", "value": expected}])

    def test_failure_is_atomic_for_both_modes(self):
        for in_place in (False, True):
            document = {"items": [1, 2]}
            original = {"items": [1, 2]}
            with self.subTest(in_place=in_place):
                with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
                    apply_patch(
                        document,
                        [
                            {"op": "remove", "path": "/items/0"},
                            {"op": "replace", "path": "/missing", "value": 3},
                        ],
                        in_place=in_place,
                    )
                self.assertEqual(document, original)

    def test_in_place_success_preserves_root_identity(self):
        document = {"items": [1, 2]}
        result = apply_patch(document, [{"op": "add", "path": "/items/-", "value": 3}], in_place=True)
        self.assertIs(result, document)
        self.assertEqual(document, {"items": [1, 2, 3]})

    def test_malformed_patch_operations_raise_patch_error(self):
        for patch in (
            {"op": "add", "path": "/x", "value": 1},
            [None],
            [{"op": "unknown", "path": ""}],
            [{"op": "add", "path": ""}],
            [{"op": "copy", "path": ""}],
            [{"op": "remove", "path": 1}],
        ):
            with self.subTest(patch=patch):
                with self.assertRaises(PatchError):
                    apply_patch({}, patch)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
